rs1801133.name: C677T
rs1801133.summary: MTHFR C677T reduces enzyme activity 40–70%, impairing conversion of folate to active methylfolate and elevating homocysteine — a cardiovascular and clotting risk factor.
rs1801133.recommendation: Use methylfolate (not folic acid) supplements. Monitor homocysteine levels. Limit alcohol. Ensure adequate riboflavin (B2), B6, and B12 intake.

cross_references.implication: MTHFR C677T impairs folate-dependent DNA synthesis and methylation in sperm, elevating sperm DNA fragmentation risk and reducing fertility. Methylfolate (not folic acid) intake supports sperm DNA integrity — particularly when trying to conceive.

Impaired methylation reduces SAMe availability and methylation-dependent metal excretion (arsenic, mercury). Carriers may need extra B-vitamin support and reduced inorganic-arsenic exposure (rice, especially brown rice from high-arsenic regions; well water testing).

rs1801131.name: A1298C
rs1801131.summary: MTHFR A1298C reduces BH4 production, affecting neurotransmitter synthesis. Compound heterozygosity with C677T (one copy of each) amplifies methylation impairment.
rs1801131.recommendation: Methylfolate and riboflavin supplementation. Extra caution if also C677T positive. Discuss homocysteine testing with your doctor.

rs1805087.name: A2756G
rs1805087.summary: MTR A2756G affects methionine synthase, an enzyme that uses B12 to regenerate methionine and recycle homocysteine. May increase need for B12.
rs1805087.recommendation: Ensure adequate methylcobalamin (active B12) intake. Consider testing serum B12 and homocysteine levels.

rs1801394.name: A66G
rs1801394.summary: MTRR A66G impairs the enzyme that reactivates methionine synthase (MTR), reducing B12-dependent methylation capacity. Often compounds with MTR A2756G.
rs1801394.recommendation: Methylcobalamin and methylfolate supplementation. Particularly important in combination with other methylation variants.

rs2236225.name: R653Q
rs2236225.summary: MTHFD1 R653Q modestly affects one-carbon metabolism and folate cycling, particularly relevant during pregnancy (neural tube defect risk).
rs2236225.recommendation: Adequate folate intake is important, especially before and during pregnancy. Methylfolate preferred over folic acid.

rs492602.name: W154X (secretor status)
rs492602.summary: FUT2 non-secretors (AA genotype) have ~50% lower serum B12 levels despite adequate intake, due to reduced B12 absorption in the gut and altered gut microbiome.
rs492602.recommendation: Non-secretors (AA) may need higher B12 supplementation. Active B12 forms (methylcobalamin, adenosylcobalamin) preferred. Test serum B12 and methylmalonic acid.

rs1801198.name: C776G
rs1801198.summary: TCN2 encodes transcobalamin II, the primary B12 transport protein. The G allele may reduce B12 delivery to cells even when serum B12 appears normal.
rs1801198.recommendation: Monitor functional B12 markers (methylmalonic acid, holotranscobalamin) rather than just serum B12. Active B12 supplementation may be more effective.

rs429358.name: E4 allele (rs429358)
rs429358.summary: rs429358 is one of two SNPs defining APOE genotype. The C allele marks the E4 haplotype. See the APOE section for combined genotype interpretation.
rs429358.recommendation: APOE genotype is interpreted by combining rs429358 and rs7412. See the APOE Genotype section of this report for full interpretation and recommendations.

rs7412.name: E2 allele (rs7412)
rs7412.summary: rs7412 is one of two SNPs defining APOE genotype. The T allele marks the E2 haplotype (protective for Alzheimer's, but associated with hyperlipoproteinemia in E2/E2).
rs7412.recommendation: APOE genotype is interpreted by combining rs429358 and rs7412. See the APOE Genotype section of this report for full interpretation and recommendations.

rs6265.name: Val66Met
rs6265.summary: BDNF Val66Met reduces activity-dependent BDNF secretion by ~30%. Associated with impaired episodic memory, increased anxiety, and modestly increased Alzheimer's risk. Also affects antidepressant response.
rs6265.recommendation: Regular aerobic exercise significantly boosts BDNF levels. Minimize chronic stress. Consider omega-3 fatty acids and curcumin (both shown to increase BDNF). Discuss with psychiatrist if on antidepressants.

cross_references.implication: BDNF Val66Met (A allele) reduces activity-dependent BDNF secretion ~30% and is associated with reduced neuroplasticity, modestly altered response to stimulants and antidepressants, and slower learning consolidation. Aerobic exercise robustly elevates BDNF; consider exercise as adjunct to any medication for cognitive/attention/mood.

rs3851179.name: rs3851179
rs3851179.summary: PICALM variant associated with modest increased Alzheimer's risk in GWAS studies. PICALM is involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis and amyloid precursor protein processing.
rs3851179.recommendation: Standard Alzheimer's prevention: regular aerobic exercise, Mediterranean diet, quality sleep, cognitive engagement, blood pressure control.

rs9331896.name: rs9331896
rs9331896.summary: CLU (Clusterin/ApoJ) variant associated with modest Alzheimer's risk. Clusterin is an extracellular chaperone involved in amyloid clearance.
rs9331896.recommendation: Preventive lifestyle measures: aerobic exercise, cognitive engagement, Mediterranean/MIND diet, quality sleep.

rs6656401.name: rs6656401
rs6656401.summary: CR1 (Complement receptor 1) variant associated with modestly increased Alzheimer's risk, possibly through impaired amyloid-beta clearance via the complement system.
rs6656401.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle (Mediterranean diet, exercise) may be particularly beneficial. Standard Alzheimer's prevention applies.

rs744373.name: rs744373
rs744373.summary: BIN1 is the second most significant Alzheimer's risk locus after APOE. Involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis and tau pathology. Effect is modest compared to APOE.
rs744373.recommendation: Standard Alzheimer's prevention. Effect is modest; lifestyle factors remain primary modifiable risk.

rs3764650.name: rs3764650
rs3764650.summary: ABCA7 rs3764650 is one of the stronger common Alzheimer's risk variants identified in GWAS (particularly in African ancestry populations). ABCA7 is involved in lipid transport and amyloid clearance.
rs3764650.recommendation: Standard Alzheimer's prevention measures: aerobic exercise, Mediterranean/MIND diet, quality sleep, cognitive engagement, blood pressure control.

rs6025.name: Factor V Leiden (R506Q)
rs6025.summary: Factor V Leiden is the most common inherited thrombophilia, causing resistance to protein C and increased clot formation risk. Heterozygotes have 5–7x higher VTE risk; homozygotes 80x higher.
rs6025.recommendation: Avoid prolonged immobilization (long flights — use compression stockings). Discuss anticoagulation risk/benefit with your hematologist. High risk periods: surgery, pregnancy, oral contraceptives (discuss alternatives with doctor). Stay hydrated and physically active.

rs1799963.name: Prothrombin G20210A
rs1799963.summary: Prothrombin G20210A increases prothrombin levels by ~30%, raising VTE (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism) risk 3–4x. Combination with Factor V Leiden further amplifies risk.
rs1799963.recommendation: Inform all physicians before surgery or hormonal therapies. Discuss prophylactic anticoagulation with a hematologist for high-risk situations. Avoid smoking. Maintain healthy weight.

rs5918.name: PlA2 (L33P)
rs5918.summary: ITGB3 PlA2 (HPA-1b) affects platelet aggregation via the fibrinogen receptor. Associated with increased risk of arterial thrombosis, MI, and stroke. Aspirin response may be reduced.
rs5918.recommendation: Discuss with cardiologist regarding aspirin efficacy. Avoid smoking. Maintain healthy blood pressure and cholesterol. If aspirin prescribed, discuss whether alternative antiplatelet therapy is warranted.

rs2289252.name: rs2289252
rs2289252.summary: Factor XI variant associated with elevated Factor XI levels and increased VTE risk. Factor XI plays a role in the intrinsic coagulation pathway.
rs2289252.recommendation: Stay hydrated and active. Inform surgeon before procedures. Similar precautions to other thrombophilia variants.

rs1800562.name: C282Y
rs1800562.summary: HFE C282Y is the primary hemochromatosis mutation. Homozygotes absorb excess dietary iron, leading to organ damage (liver, heart, joints, pancreas). Heterozygotes have mildly elevated iron.
rs1800562.recommendation: Get serum ferritin and transferrin saturation tested. If elevated: therapeutic phlebotomy is the treatment. Avoid iron supplements and vitamin C supplements with meals (enhances iron absorption). Limit red meat and alcohol. Discuss regular monitoring with your doctor.

cross_references.implication: HFE C282Y carriers absorb excess iron, and iron overload promotes oxidative stress and impairs cadmium/lead handling (transport-pathway competition). Manage iron status (ferritin <100 ng/mL ideal in C282Y+); avoid iron supplements and high-dose vitamin C with meals.

rs1799945.name: H63D
rs1799945.summary: HFE H63D is a milder hemochromatosis mutation. Most H63D heterozygotes are unaffected; compound heterozygosity with C282Y increases risk. Homozygotes have mildly elevated iron stores.
rs1799945.recommendation: Monitor ferritin and transferrin saturation periodically, especially if C282Y positive. Moderate red meat intake. Avoid iron supplements unless deficient.

rs855791.name: V736A
rs855791.summary: TMPRSS6 V736A reduces hepcidin suppression and lowers iron absorption, predisposing to iron deficiency anemia — especially in women with heavy menstrual cycles.
rs855791.recommendation: Monitor CBC and ferritin, especially in premenopausal women. Ensure adequate dietary iron (heme iron best absorbed). Vitamin C with iron-rich meals enhances absorption. Discuss with doctor if fatigued or anemic.

rs7385804.name: rs7385804 (Transferrin)
rs7385804.summary: Transferrin variant modestly associated with iron transport capacity and may influence iron status. Interactions with HFE variants are relevant.
rs7385804.recommendation: No specific action needed alone. Monitor iron stores if combined with other iron metabolism variants.

rs7903146.name: rs7903146
rs7903146.summary: TCF7L2 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for Type 2 diabetes. The T allele impairs insulin secretion and incretin response. Each T allele increases T2D risk ~40%.
rs7903146.recommendation: Prioritize low-glycemic diet, regular aerobic exercise (150 min/week), and healthy weight. Monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c. The T allele may predict better response to certain diabetes medications (GLP-1 agonists). Discuss screening schedule with doctor.

rs12255372.name: rs12255372
rs12255372.summary: Second TCF7L2 T2D risk variant. When combined with rs7903146, substantially increases diabetes risk. Effect is through impaired beta-cell function and incretin signaling.
rs12255372.recommendation: Same as rs7903146: low-glycemic diet, regular exercise, weight management, glucose monitoring.

rs5219.name: E23K
rs5219.summary: KCNJ11 E23K encodes the Kir6.2 subunit of the pancreatic ATP-sensitive potassium channel. The K allele impairs insulin secretion and increases T2D risk ~15% per allele.
rs5219.recommendation: Regular glucose monitoring. Low-sugar diet. KCNJ11 affects response to sulfonylurea medications — inform prescriber of this variant.

rs1801282.name: Pro12Ala
rs1801282.summary: PPARG Pro12Ala: the G allele (Ala) is actually protective against T2D and obesity in most populations. The common C allele (Pro12) is associated with modestly increased insulin resistance.
rs1801282.recommendation: Healthy fat intake (monounsaturated fats particularly beneficial for PPARG). Regular exercise. PPARG is the target of thiazolidinedione diabetes drugs.

cross_references.implication: PPARG P12A (the G allele, Ala12) is associated with modestly improved insulin sensitivity, lower risk of type 2 diabetes, and somewhat lower body weight — particularly in the context of monounsaturated-fat-rich diets (Mediterranean-style). Favorable allele. Continue Mediterranean-style eating (olive oil, nuts, fish, vegetables); these foods particularly benefit P12A carriers.

rs9939609.name: rs9939609
rs9939609.summary: FTO rs9939609 is strongly associated with obesity and T2D risk. The A allele increases BMI by ~0.4 kg/m² and obesity risk ~1.3x per allele, via effects on appetite regulation and energy metabolism.
rs9939609.recommendation: High-protein, low-glycemic diet. Regular aerobic exercise (notably attenuates FTO genetic risk). Prioritize sleep (sleep deprivation amplifies FTO risk). Structured meal timing helps.

cross_references.implication: FTO rs9939609 A allele is the most replicated common variant for body mass — each copy adds ~1 kg of weight on average via increased food intake and reduced satiety. Indirectly increases cardiovascular risk via obesity, diabetes, hypertension. Effect is fully overcome by adequate physical activity (≥150 min/week vigorous + resistance training). Higher-protein diets (≥1.6 g/kg/day) improve satiety in carriers. Mindful/structured eating helps offset diminished satiety signalling.

rs1387153.name: rs1387153
rs1387153.summary: MTNR1B encodes the melatonin receptor. The T allele impairs insulin secretion in response to meals, particularly in the evening when melatonin is elevated — making evening meal timing especially important.
rs1387153.recommendation: Avoid eating late at night (2–3 hours before sleep). Keep consistent meal timing. This variant responds particularly well to time-restricted eating (earlier eating window).

rs13266634.name: R325W
rs13266634.summary: SLC30A8 R325W affects zinc transport in pancreatic beta cells, impairing insulin crystallization and secretion. Associated with ~15% increased T2D risk.
rs13266634.recommendation: Adequate zinc intake important (oysters, red meat, seeds, legumes). Zinc supplementation may be beneficial. Moderate carbohydrate diet.

rs3892097.name: *4 (poor metabolizer)
rs3892097.summary: CYP2D6 *4 is the most common poor-metabolizer allele in Europeans (~20–25% carrier rate). CYP2D6 metabolizes ~25% of all drugs including codeine, tramadol, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and beta-blockers.
rs3892097.recommendation: CRITICAL: Inform all prescribers you may be a CYP2D6 poor metabolizer. Codeine and tramadol should be avoided (no conversion to active form). Many antidepressants and antipsychotics require dose adjustment. Request CYP pharmacogenomics testing before starting new medications.

rs4244285.name: *2 (poor metabolizer)
rs4244285.summary: CYP2C19 *2 is a non-functional allele affecting metabolism of clopidogrel (Plavix), PPIs (omeprazole), antidepressants, and antifungals. Poor metabolizers on clopidogrel have higher cardiovascular event risk.
rs4244285.recommendation: CRITICAL: If prescribed clopidogrel (Plavix) for heart disease, this variant significantly reduces drug effectiveness. Alternative antiplatelet therapy may be needed. PPI doses may need adjustment. Discuss CYP2C19 testing with your cardiologist and pharmacist.

rs4986893.name: *3 (poor metabolizer)
rs4986893.summary: CYP2C19 *3 is a non-functional allele common in Asian populations (rare in Europeans). Combined with *2, creates a complete CYP2C19 poor metabolizer phenotype with significant drug interaction implications.
rs4986893.recommendation: Same implications as CYP2C19 *2: clopidogrel, PPIs, and several antidepressants affected. Inform prescribers. CYP2C19 pharmacogenomics testing recommended.

rs762551.name: *1F (rapid caffeine metabolizer)
rs762551.summary: CYP1A2 *1F (A allele) is induced by smoking and determines caffeine metabolism speed. Rapid metabolizers (AA + smoker/exerciser) clear caffeine faster; slow metabolizers retain caffeine longer with higher cardiovascular risk from high intake.
rs762551.recommendation: Slow metabolizers (CC): limit caffeine to 1–2 cups/day; avoid caffeine after noon; higher risk of MI at high intake. Rapid metabolizers (AA): generally more caffeine-tolerant. CYP1A2 also metabolizes several medications — inform prescribers.

cross_references.implication: CYP1A2 *1F (C allele) is the slow-caffeine-metabolizer variant. Slow metabolizers (C/C, ~10% of population) clear caffeine ~50% more slowly — coffee may worsen anxiety, sleep, and is associated in some studies with elevated MI risk among slow metabolizers. Slow metabolizers: limit caffeine after noon, keep total intake ≤200 mg/day, consider switching to decaf or tea (lower caffeine). Fast metabolizers (A/A) tolerate more coffee and may actually derive cardioprotection from moderate intake.

rs1799853.name: *2 (reduced function)
rs1799853.summary: CYP2C9 *2 reduces warfarin, NSAIDs, and phenytoin metabolism. Reduced function carriers require lower warfarin doses and are at higher bleeding risk at standard doses.
rs1799853.recommendation: If prescribed warfarin, this variant affects your optimal dose. Always inform prescribers. CYP2C9 *2 combined with VKORC1 variants further alters warfarin requirements. Clinical pharmacogenomics testing recommended before starting warfarin.

rs1057910.name: *3 (poor function)
rs1057910.summary: CYP2C9 *3 severely reduces enzyme function. *3/*3 homozygotes metabolize warfarin at <5% normal rate and require very low doses. Also affects NSAIDs (higher GI bleeding risk) and many other drugs.
rs1057910.recommendation: CRITICAL: Warfarin requires markedly reduced doses if you carry *3 alleles. Routine NSAIDs may carry higher bleeding risk. Phenytoin and several diabetes drugs also affected. Comprehensive pharmacogenomics panel strongly recommended.

rs4149056.name: V174A (*5)
rs4149056.summary: SLCO1B1 V174A reduces hepatic uptake of statins, causing up to 5x higher plasma statin concentrations. Strongly associated with statin-induced myopathy (muscle damage), especially with simvastatin.
rs4149056.recommendation: CRITICAL: If prescribed statins, this variant significantly increases myopathy risk. Simvastatin and high-dose lovastatin should be avoided. Rosuvastatin and pravastatin are safer choices. Start with lowest effective statin dose. Report muscle pain/weakness immediately to your doctor.

rs9923231.name: -1639G>A
rs9923231.summary: VKORC1 -1639G>A is the primary determinant of warfarin sensitivity. The A allele (T on forward strand) reduces VKORC1 expression, requiring substantially lower warfarin doses to achieve anticoagulation.
rs9923231.recommendation: CRITICAL: This variant significantly affects warfarin dosing. Required dose can be 30–50% lower than standard. Combined with CYP2C9 variants, predictive algorithms calculate personalized warfarin doses. Never start warfarin without informing prescriber of this variant.

rs2108622.name: V433M
rs2108622.summary: CYP4F2 V433M affects vitamin K metabolism and warfarin requirements. The T allele reduces vitamin K1 oxidation, requiring slightly higher warfarin doses — opposite to VKORC1 effect.
rs2108622.recommendation: Warfarin dosing algorithms should incorporate CYP4F2 alongside VKORC1 and CYP2C9 for best precision. Inform prescribers of this variant.

rs1045642.name: C3435T (MDR1)
rs1045642.summary: ABCB1 C3435T affects P-glycoprotein, a drug efflux pump. The TT genotype is associated with higher drug bioavailability for many medications (digoxin, HIV antiretrovirals, tacrolimus, fexofenadine).
rs1045642.recommendation: Inform prescribers, particularly for medications with narrow therapeutic windows. Effect varies by drug — pharmacogenomics consultation is worthwhile if on multiple medications.

rs1142345.name: *3C (Y240C)
rs1142345.summary: TPMT *3C causes thiopurine S-methyltransferase deficiency. Carriers receiving azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, or thioguanine (for autoimmune disease, organ transplant, or childhood leukemia) are at severe myelosuppression risk.
rs1142345.recommendation: CRITICAL: If prescribed azathioprine, 6-MP, or thioguanine, TPMT status is essential for dosing. Poor metabolizers require 10-fold dose reductions. Inform all prescribers — especially rheumatologists, gastroenterologists, and oncologists.

rs1800460.name: *3B (G460A)
rs1800460.summary: TPMT *3B, when combined with *3C (rs1142345), creates the *3A allele — the most common non-functional TPMT allele. Same clinical implications as *3C.
rs1800460.recommendation: Same as TPMT *3C: critical to inform prescribers before any thiopurine therapy. Genetic testing for TPMT is standard of care before these medications.

rs4148323.name: *28 promoter variant
rs4148323.summary: UGT1A1 *28 reduces bilirubin conjugation (associated with Gilbert's syndrome). Also slows irinotecan (chemotherapy) metabolism, causing severe toxicity risk in homozygotes (*28/*28).
rs4148323.recommendation: Elevated bilirubin (jaundice) during illness/fasting is usually benign in Gilbert's syndrome. If ever prescribed irinotecan for cancer, inform oncologist of this variant — dose reduction required in *28/*28. Some antiretrovirals (atazanavir, indinavir) also affected.

rs3745274.name: *6 (Q172H/K262R)
rs3745274.summary: CYP2B6 *6 is the primary determinant of efavirenz (HIV medication) metabolism. Slow metabolizers have 3–4x higher efavirenz plasma levels, causing neuropsychiatric side effects. Also affects bupropion and cyclophosphamide.
rs3745274.recommendation: If prescribed efavirenz (HIV treatment) or bupropion (antidepressant/smoking cessation), this variant requires dose adjustment. Inform prescribers. Common in African populations (~45% allele frequency).

rs1815739.name: R577X
rs1815739.summary: ACTN3 R577X (TT = XX genotype, no alpha-actinin-3 protein) shifts muscle toward oxidative/endurance phenotype. TT individuals excel at endurance sports; CC (RR) individuals have more fast-twitch fibers for power/sprint performance.
rs1815739.recommendation: TT (XX): optimize endurance training — marathon, cycling, triathlon. CC (RR): natural advantage in power/sprint sports. CT (RX): intermediate profile. Training type may matter more than genetics for most people.

rs1799752.name: I/D (insertion/deletion)
rs1799752.summary: ACE I/D polymorphism: the I (insertion) allele is associated with lower ACE activity and endurance performance; the D (deletion) allele with higher ACE activity and power/strength performance. This proxy SNP captures the I/D effect.
rs1799752.recommendation: I allele carriers: may have endurance advantages. D allele carriers: may have strength/power advantages. ACE inhibitor medications may be slightly more effective in I allele carriers.

rs8192678.name: Gly482Ser
rs8192678.summary: PPARGC1A Gly482Ser affects PGC-1alpha, the master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis. The Ser (A) allele is associated with reduced mitochondrial density, lower VO2max response to training, and increased T2D risk.
rs8192678.recommendation: High-volume aerobic training is particularly important for Ser allele carriers to maximize mitochondrial adaptations. Cold exposure and caloric restriction also stimulate PGC-1alpha. Creatine supplementation may help offset reduced power output.

rs1053049.name: intron 7 variant
rs1053049.summary: PPARA (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha) regulates fatty acid oxidation and is expressed highly in endurance-trained muscle. Variants associated with endurance performance.
rs1053049.recommendation: No specific action needed. General endurance training recommendations apply.

rs34602416.name: Q12X (myoadenylate deaminase deficiency)
rs34602416.summary: AMPD1 Q12X causes myoadenylate deaminase deficiency. Carriers (~2% of Europeans are homozygous) may experience exercise-related muscle cramps and fatigue. Paradoxically, some studies show reduced cardiovascular risk.
rs34602416.recommendation: If experiencing exercise-related muscle cramps and fatigue without other explanation, AMPD1 deficiency may be contributing. D-ribose supplementation has some evidence for improving exercise tolerance. Consult a sports medicine physician.

rs174537.name: rs174537
rs174537.summary: FADS1 regulates fatty acid desaturation (conversion of ALA to EPA/DHA). The T allele reduces conversion efficiency, meaning plant-based omega-3s (ALA from flaxseed, chia) are less effectively converted to EPA and DHA.
rs174537.recommendation: T allele carriers should prioritize preformed EPA/DHA from marine sources (fatty fish, algae-based omega-3 supplements) rather than relying on plant-based ALA conversion.

rs174547.name: rs174547
rs174547.summary: FADS1 rs174547 affects omega-3/omega-6 fatty acid conversion. T allele reduces conversion efficiency, lowering plasma EPA and DHA from plant-source ALA.
rs174547.recommendation: Prioritize marine omega-3 sources (fatty fish, algae-based DHA/EPA supplements). Plant-based ALA (flaxseed, chia) is less effective for this genotype.

rs4988235.name: C/T-13910 (lactase persistence)
rs4988235.summary: LCT rs4988235 determines adult lactase activity. The A allele confers lactase persistence (dairy tolerance). GG genotype = primary lactase non-persistence (lactose intolerance) in ~65–70% of adults globally.
rs4988235.recommendation: GG (lactose intolerant): limit lactose-containing dairy or use lactase enzyme supplements. Aged cheeses and yogurt have lower lactose. Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D from other sources. GA: usually tolerates moderate dairy.

cross_references.implication: Note: this is the lactase persistence variant — included here as it's commonly observed; not primarily an eye health variant. T allele = lactase persistence (most Europeans). C/C = lactase non-persistence (lactose intolerance after weaning). If C/C: limit dairy or use lactase-pretreated dairy. Yogurt and aged cheeses are usually well tolerated. Adequate calcium and vitamin D from non-dairy sources if avoiding dairy.

rs2228570.name: Fok1 (C>T, Ala/Val)
rs2228570.summary: VDR Fok1 affects vitamin D receptor protein length and transcriptional activity. The T allele (shorter VDR) is associated with reduced vitamin D signaling efficiency, higher cancer risk, and immune dysregulation.
rs2228570.recommendation: Maintain higher serum 25(OH)D levels (aim for 40–60 ng/mL). Supplementation with vitamin D3 2000–4000 IU/day often needed. Magnesium is required for vitamin D activation — ensure adequate intake.

cross_references.implication: VDR (vitamin D receptor) FokI rs2228570 T allele (f variant) produces a slightly less transcriptionally active VDR. Associated with reduced muscle strength response to training and lower bone mineral density in some studies. Ensure vitamin D sufficiency (25-OH-D 30–50 ng/mL). Resistance training 2–3× /week. Adequate protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg/day for active individuals).

rs731236.name: Taq1 (T/C)
rs731236.summary: VDR Taq1 is another common vitamin D receptor variant associated with bone density, cancer susceptibility, and immune function. Often analyzed together with Fok1 and Bsm1.
rs731236.recommendation: Maintain adequate vitamin D levels (test 25(OH)D). Calcium and vitamin D3 together for bone health.

rs7041.name: D416E (Vitamin D binding protein)
rs7041.summary: GC encodes the vitamin D binding protein (VDBP), which transports vitamin D in blood. Variants affect serum 25(OH)D levels and bioavailable vitamin D, independent of supplementation.
rs7041.recommendation: Test serum 25(OH)D. May need higher supplementation doses to achieve optimal levels. Discuss with doctor — 'bioavailable' or 'free' vitamin D testing may be more informative than total 25(OH)D.

rs12934922.name: A379V
rs12934922.summary: BCMO1 A379V reduces beta-carotene to vitamin A conversion by ~57%. Carriers relying on plant-based vitamin A (beta-carotene from carrots, sweet potatoes) may become vitamin A deficient.
rs12934922.recommendation: Include preformed vitamin A from animal sources (liver, egg yolks, dairy) or use retinol supplements. Heavy beta-carotene supplementation from plant sources may be insufficient. Test vitamin A status if on a strictly plant-based diet.

rs7501331.name: R267S
rs7501331.summary: Second BCMO1 variant affecting beta-carotene conversion. The two BCMO1 variants together can reduce conversion by up to 90% in some individuals.
rs7501331.recommendation: If carrying both BCMO1 variants, plant-source beta-carotene is nearly useless as a vitamin A source. Preformed vitamin A is essential. Avoid very high beta-carotene supplementation (no conversion benefit, and possible carotenemia).

rs17782313.name: rs17782313
rs17782313.summary: MC4R is a key appetite regulator in the hypothalamus. The C allele is associated with increased food intake, preference for high-fat foods, and ~1.3x higher obesity risk per allele.
rs17782313.recommendation: High-protein diet (improves satiety via melanocortin signaling). Structured meal timing and portion control. Regular aerobic exercise. Avoid high-fat processed foods. Sleep deprivation significantly worsens appetite dysregulation in MC4R variants.

cross_references.implication: MC4R rs17782313 C allele is associated with higher BMI, increased food intake, and modestly elevated cardiometabolic risk. MC4R is the central melanocortin appetite-regulation hub; rare loss-of-function MC4R mutations cause severe early-onset obesity. Same strategies as rs9939609: higher-protein diet, structured eating, physical activity. For severe early-onset obesity in family history, ask about MC4R coding-variant screening — setmelanotide is approved for some MC4R-pathway deficiencies.

rs1761667.name: rs1761667
rs1761667.summary: CD36 affects fat taste sensitivity. The A allele is associated with reduced fat taste detection, potentially leading to higher fat intake for taste satisfaction.
rs1761667.recommendation: Be mindful of fat intake if food satisfaction is driving excess consumption. Mindful eating practices and cooking with healthy fats (olive oil, avocado) may help.

rs4680.name: Val158Met
rs4680.summary: COMT Val158Met determines dopamine clearance speed in the prefrontal cortex. Met/Met (AA): low COMT activity, higher dopamine — better cognitive performance under calm conditions, but worse under stress ('worriers'). Val/Val (GG): high COMT activity, lower dopamine — better stress resilience but less optimal cognition ('warriors').
rs4680.recommendation: Met/Met (AA): avoid extreme stress; mindfulness meditation helps; be cautious with stimulants and excess methyl donors (SAMe, high-dose methylfolate can worsen). Val/Val (GG): tyrosine-rich foods (lean meat, eggs) may support dopamine. Both: exercise boosts prefrontal dopamine. COMT significantly affects antidepressant and antipsychotic response — inform prescribers.

cross_references.implication: Val/Val (G/G) clears synaptic dopamine fastest — may need higher Vyvanse / amphetamine doses for the same effect, but typically tolerates stimulants well. Met/Met (A/A) clears dopamine slowest — more sensitive to stimulants, may have more anxiety / over-stimulation side effects. Heterozygotes are intermediate. STRONG DISCLAIMER: medication choice and dosing must involve a psychiatrist.

COMT also methylates catechol estrogens — slow COMT (Met/Met) carriers clear 2-OH and 4-OH estrogens more slowly, with implications for estrogen-driven cancer risk in women and overall estrogen balance. Magnesium and methylation cofactors support COMT activity.

rs1800497.name: Taq1A (A1 allele)
rs1800497.summary: DRD2 Taq1A (A1 allele = T) is associated with reduced striatal dopamine D2 receptor density (~30% reduction). Linked to reward deficiency syndrome: higher addiction risk, ADHD, overeating, compulsive behaviors.
rs1800497.recommendation: Be mindful of addictive behaviors (substances, gambling, overeating). Regular aerobic exercise significantly upregulates dopamine receptors. Reward-rich goals and positive reinforcement structures are particularly important. Discuss ADHD evaluation if relevant.

cross_references.implication: DRD2 Taq1A A1 allele (T) is associated with ~30–40% lower striatal D2 receptor density and altered reward signalling. May affect response to stimulants and is linked with addictive behaviors. Stimulant treatment should be monitored for rebound, craving, and tolerance — discuss with prescriber.

rs25531.name: 5-HTTLPR (serotonin transporter)
rs25531.summary: SLC6A4 5-HTTLPR affects serotonin transporter expression. The short allele (S, tagged by G) reduces serotonin reuptake capacity and is associated with anxiety, depression vulnerability, and SSRI response variability.
rs25531.recommendation: S-allele carriers: particularly benefit from stress-management practices (mindfulness, CBT). Aerobic exercise is especially beneficial. Serotonin-rich diet (tryptophan in turkey, eggs, dairy). SSRIs may be particularly effective — discuss with psychiatrist.

rs4570625.name: rs4570625
rs4570625.summary: TPH2 is the rate-limiting enzyme in brain serotonin synthesis. The G allele is associated with reduced serotonin production and modestly increased depression and anxiety risk.
rs4570625.recommendation: Tryptophan-rich foods and 5-HTP may support serotonin production. Sunlight exposure and exercise are among the strongest evidence-based serotonin boosters.

rs6323.name: MAOA-uVNTR (high/low activity)
rs6323.summary: MAOA degrades serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine. The high-activity variant (this SNP is a proxy) clears monoamines rapidly — associated with resilience but possibly blunted reward. Low-activity variant retains monoamines longer — increased risk for impulsivity/aggression under adversity.
rs6323.recommendation: Low-activity MAOA carriers should particularly focus on stress management, avoiding adverse childhood environments' downstream effects, and regular exercise. High-activity: consider if medications that rely on MAO inhibition (MAOIs) are being used.

rs1799971.name: A118G
rs1799971.summary: OPRM1 A118G affects the mu-opioid receptor. The G allele is associated with higher receptor binding affinity, increased endorphin response to social connection, higher alcohol reward, and reduced opioid analgesic requirements.
rs1799971.recommendation: G allele carriers: stronger response to social bonding activities (relationships are powerful medicine). May require lower opioid analgesic doses for pain — inform anesthesiologist/pain specialist. Higher alcohol reward sensation — be mindful of alcohol habits.

cross_references.implication: OPRM1 A118G G allele alters opioid receptor binding — has been associated with altered response to alcohol, opioids, and stimulant-related reward processing. Worth flagging for any prescriber considering opioids or naltrexone.

rs1800955.name: C521T (exon 3 promoter)
rs1800955.summary: DRD4 variant associated with novelty-seeking and ADHD. DRD4 exon 3 VNTR variants (particularly 7-repeat) are more directly studied for ADHD; this promoter variant has modest but independent associations.
rs1800955.recommendation: No specific action needed for this variant alone. Combined with other dopamine variants, may inform understanding of reward processing and ADHD tendencies.

rs1495741.name: rs1495741 (slow acetylator)
rs1495741.summary: NAT2 slow acetylators (AA) cannot efficiently detoxify aromatic amines from cigarette smoke, grilled meats, and certain drugs. Associated with 2–3x higher bladder cancer risk in smokers and adverse reactions to isoniazid, hydralazine, and procainamide.
rs1495741.recommendation: Do not smoke. Minimize consumption of well-done/charred meat. If prescribed isoniazid (TB treatment), hydralazine, or procainamide: slow acetylators need dose reductions to prevent drug toxicity. Inform prescribers.

cross_references.implication: NAT2 'slow acetylator' phenotype is associated with increased susceptibility to aromatic amine carcinogens (some industrial chemicals, charred meat, cigarette smoke), bladder cancer risk, and altered drug metabolism (isoniazid, sulfonamides). Reduce occupational/environmental aromatic-amine exposure; minimize charred meat; don't smoke.

rs1801280.name: I114T (slow acetylator)
rs1801280.summary: Second NAT2 slow acetylator variant. Compound with rs1495741 to determine complete acetylator phenotype. Important for drug metabolism and carcinogen clearance.
rs1801280.recommendation: Same as rs1495741: avoid smoking, limit charred meats, inform prescribers of NAT2 slow acetylator status before relevant medications.

rs671.name: E504K (Glu504Lys)
rs671.summary: ALDH2 *2 (E504K) is common in East Asians (~30–40% carrier rate). Causes alcohol flush reaction (flushing, nausea, tachycardia). Dramatically increases esophageal and head/neck cancer risk in drinkers — 6–10x higher risk per drink compared to non-carriers. ALDH2 also critical for cardiac protection.
rs671.recommendation: CRITICAL: Avoid or strictly limit alcohol consumption. If drinking causes flushing, this is the biological mechanism — the flushing is NOT just cosmetic but indicates toxic acetaldehyde accumulation. Regular cardiac evaluation is beneficial. ALDH2 activators (Alda-1) are in research trials.

rs1229984.name: Arg47His (His48Arg)
rs1229984.summary: ADH1B Arg47His: the G allele (His47) dramatically speeds alcohol oxidation to acetaldehyde. This is actually protective against alcoholism (fast acetaldehyde buildup is aversive) but increases cancer risk in people who drink despite the reaction.
rs1229984.recommendation: G allele carriers: if you drink and notice flushing/discomfort, this is biologically based. The protective effect against alcoholism is strongest in Asian populations. Limit alcohol consumption.

rs4880.name: Ala16Val (MnSOD)
rs4880.summary: SOD2 Ala16Val affects mitochondrial superoxide dismutase targeting. The Val (T) allele impairs SOD2 transport into mitochondria, reducing antioxidant capacity and increasing oxidative stress, particularly relevant for cancer risk and exercise recovery.
rs4880.recommendation: Antioxidant-rich diet (colorful vegetables, berries). CoQ10 supplementation supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense. Avoid smoking and excessive alcohol. Adequate sleep for oxidative stress recovery. Consider additional antioxidants (lipoic acid, selenium).

cross_references.implication: SOD2 V16A (the slow/Ala variant) reduces mitochondrial antioxidant capacity. Sperm have abundant mitochondria for motility; reduced SOD2 activity increases oxidative damage to sperm DNA and motility apparatus. Supplement CoQ10 200 mg/day, selenium 100–200 µg/day, vitamin E if trying to conceive.

Heavy metals (cadmium, mercury, lead) inflict mitochondrial oxidative damage. Reduced SOD2 activity worsens vulnerability. Pair detox-pathway support with antioxidant cofactors (NAC, glutathione precursors, vitamin C/E, selenium).

rs1695.name: Ile105Val
rs1695.summary: GSTP1 Ile105Val reduces glutathione S-transferase activity, impairing conjugation and elimination of toxins, carcinogens, and reactive oxygen species. Associated with increased lung and breast cancer risk.
rs1695.recommendation: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts) are potent GSTP1 inducers — eat daily. Avoid tobacco smoke and environmental toxins. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supports glutathione production. Minimize pesticide exposure.

cross_references.implication: GSTP1 I105V (G allele = Val variant) modulates glutathione conjugation in reproductive tissue. Sperm are vulnerable to oxidative damage; reduced GSTP1 activity is associated with higher sperm DNA fragmentation. Support with NAC, selenium, glutathione precursors when trying to conceive.

GSTP1 is part of phase II detoxification of metal-induced electrophiles and many xenobiotics. Reduced activity (V allele) is associated with worse outcomes after environmental exposures. NAC, cruciferous vegetables, and sulforaphane upregulate compensatory pathways.

rs1800566.name: Pro187Ser
rs1800566.summary: NQO1 Pro187Ser causes a near-complete loss of NQO1 enzyme activity (TT = <2% activity). NQO1 is critical for preventing quinone toxicity and maintaining antioxidant CoQ10. Associated with increased benzene sensitivity and some cancer risks.
rs1800566.recommendation: Minimize benzene exposure (gasoline fumes, cigarette smoke). CoQ10 supplementation is particularly important (NQO1 recycles CoQ10). Resveratrol and sulforaphane (broccoli) induce other protective pathways. Avoid prolonged benzene/solvent exposure occupationally.

rs1800629.name: -308G/A
rs1800629.summary: TNF-alpha -308G/A increases TNF-alpha production 6–7x. Associated with elevated baseline inflammation, autoimmune diseases, sepsis severity, and chronic inflammatory conditions.
rs1800629.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory diet (Mediterranean). Regular moderate exercise. Avoid smoking. Adequate sleep. Consider omega-3 supplementation and curcumin.

cross_references.implication: Higher TNF-α from -308A carriage contributes to inflammatory milieu in the testicular environment — may impair spermatogenesis when combined with other oxidative-stress factors. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle (Mediterranean diet, omega-3, exercise, weight management) particularly relevant if fertility is a goal.

rs1800795.name: -174G/C
rs1800795.summary: IL-6 -174G/C: the C allele is associated with lower IL-6 production in some tissues (paradoxically higher in some conditions). IL-6 is a pleiotropic cytokine with roles in acute inflammation, immune response, and metabolic regulation.
rs1800795.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle: Mediterranean diet, regular moderate exercise, adequate sleep. IL-6 is elevated by obesity, smoking, and sedentary lifestyle — all modifiable. Discuss high-sensitivity CRP testing with doctor.

cross_references.implication: IL-6 -174 C/C is associated with lower IL-6 and 'inflammaging' tone. Lower chronic inflammation is associated with longer lifespan. Continue anti-inflammatory lifestyle: Mediterranean diet, exercise, sleep, stress management, healthy body composition.

rs16944.name: -511C/T
rs16944.summary: IL-1B -511C/T increases interleukin-1 beta production, a potent pro-inflammatory cytokine. Associated with H. pylori-related gastric cancer, inflammatory bowel risk, and general inflammatory disease susceptibility.
rs16944.recommendation: H. pylori testing if gastrointestinal symptoms present. Anti-inflammatory diet. Avoid NSAIDs chronically (may exacerbate gut inflammation). Omega-3 fatty acids. Discuss with gastroenterologist if GI symptoms persist.

rs1143634.name: +3953C/T
rs1143634.summary: IL-1B +3953C/T increases IL-1 beta production and is associated with increased severity of periodontal disease, joint inflammation, and systemic inflammatory conditions.
rs1143634.recommendation: Excellent dental hygiene (periodontitis significantly raises systemic inflammation). Anti-inflammatory diet. Regular exercise. Combine with IL-1B -511 for full inflammatory picture.

rs1800896.name: -1082G/A
rs1800896.summary: IL-10 -1082G/A: the A allele is associated with reduced IL-10 (anti-inflammatory cytokine) production, resulting in less counter-regulation of inflammation. Associated with autoimmune disease risk and worse outcomes in infection.
rs1800896.recommendation: Particularly important to maintain anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Probiotics support gut IL-10 production. Omega-3 fatty acids. Sleep deprivation reduces IL-10 — prioritize sleep quality.

rs4073.name: -251A/T
rs4073.summary: IL-8 -251A/T variant associated with increased IL-8 (CXCL8) production, which recruits neutrophils to sites of inflammation. Associated with gastric cancer risk (especially combined with H. pylori) and inflammatory conditions.
rs4073.recommendation: H. pylori testing if warranted. Anti-inflammatory diet and lifestyle.

rs2430561.name: +874A/T
rs2430561.summary: IFN-gamma +874A/T: the T allele is associated with higher IFN-gamma production and a more robust Th1 immune response. The A allele may impair anti-mycobacterial immunity and tumor surveillance.
rs2430561.recommendation: Adequate vitamin D (strongly regulates IFN-gamma pathway). Regular moderate exercise for immune optimization.

rs7574865.name: rs7574865
rs7574865.summary: STAT4 rs7574865 (T allele) is associated with increased risk of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, type 1 diabetes, and other autoimmune diseases. STAT4 mediates IL-12 and IFN-gamma signaling in immune cells.
rs7574865.recommendation: Discuss rheumatological screening with your doctor if experiencing joint pain, fatigue, or other autoimmune symptoms. Anti-inflammatory diet and stress management. Vitamin D supplementation supports immune regulation.

cross_references.implication: STAT4 rs7574865 T allele is associated with autoimmune diseases — lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, Sjögren's. Effect size is modest. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Vitamin D sufficiency. If signs/symptoms of autoimmune disease (joint swelling, persistent fatigue, rashes), see a rheumatologist.

rs2476601.name: R620W
rs2476601.summary: PTPN22 R620W is one of the strongest autoimmune risk variants in Europeans. The A allele impairs T-cell receptor signaling regulation, increasing risk of rheumatoid arthritis (~2x), type 1 diabetes (~1.7x), lupus, Graves' disease, and myasthenia gravis.
rs2476601.recommendation: Discuss autoimmune disease screening with your doctor. Early detection of RA or T1D is clinically important. Vitamin D optimization supports immune regulation. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Stress management is critical (stress triggers autoimmune flares).

rs2187668.name: DQ2.5 celiac risk allele
rs2187668.summary: This HLA-DQA1 variant is one of two primary genetic markers for celiac disease susceptibility (HLA-DQ2 haplotype). ~95% of celiac patients carry HLA-DQ2 or DQ8. Presence does not guarantee celiac disease — only 3% of carriers develop it.
rs2187668.recommendation: If experiencing digestive symptoms, fatigue, or nutritional deficiencies: get tested for celiac disease (serum tTG-IgA first). Do NOT go gluten-free before testing — it invalidates results. If negative, periodic monitoring may be warranted especially with gastrointestinal symptoms.

rs7775228.name: DQ2/DQ8 celiac risk allele
rs7775228.summary: Second HLA variant contributing to celiac disease susceptibility via the DQ2 haplotype. Used in combination with rs2187668 for genetic celiac risk assessment.
rs7775228.recommendation: See rs2187668 recommendations. Full HLA-DQ typing by a clinical genetics lab provides more definitive celiac susceptibility assessment.

rs3184504.name: R262W
rs3184504.summary: SH2B3 (LNK) R262W is a pleiotropic variant associated with celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, hypothyroidism, and interestingly, better outcomes in myeloproliferative disorders.
rs3184504.recommendation: Discuss with doctor if autoimmune conditions run in the family. Thyroid function testing (TSH) is reasonable. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle.

rs333.name: Delta32 (32 bp deletion)
rs333.summary: CCR5 Delta32 deletion confers resistance to HIV-1 infection in homozygotes (del/del, ~1% of Europeans) and slower AIDS progression in heterozygotes. However, it may increase susceptibility to West Nile virus and certain other infections.
rs333.recommendation: del/del carriers are highly resistant to CCR5-tropic HIV. This is the basis for gene therapy approaches (Berlin Patient). Standard safe-sex practices still important (some HIV strains use CXCR4 instead). Inform your doctor of this variant.

rs80338939.name: 35delG (W24X)
rs80338939.summary: GJB2 35delG is the most common cause of hereditary non-syndromic sensorineural hearing loss (connexin 26). Heterozygotes are carriers; homozygotes or compound heterozygotes (with other GJB2 variants) develop congenital hearing loss.
rs80338939.recommendation: Heterozygous carriers: consider genetic counseling before family planning (25% chance of deaf child if partner is also a carrier). Homozygotes: hearing loss is expected — audiological evaluation and hearing aid/cochlear implant evaluation is essential.

rs1801260.name: T3111C
rs1801260.summary: CLOCK T3111C affects the core circadian clock gene. The C allele is associated with evening chronotype ('night owl'), delayed sleep phase, insomnia, reduced sleep duration, and increased susceptibility to seasonal mood changes.
rs1801260.recommendation: C allele carriers: prioritize consistent sleep schedule (same bedtime/wake time). Morning bright light exposure helps reset circadian rhythm. Limit blue light after 9pm. Melatonin 0.5mg 1–2 hours before desired sleep time may help. Avoid late caffeine.

rs228697.name: 5-repeat VNTR (proxy)
rs228697.summary: PER3 VNTR (5-repeat allele, approximated by this proxy SNP) is associated with extreme morning chronotype, increased sleep pressure, and greater vulnerability to sleep deprivation cognitive effects.
rs228697.recommendation: 5-repeat carriers: sleep deprivation hits you harder than average — 8 hours is particularly important. Morning chronotype: leverage this with early workout and high-cognitive-demand tasks in the morning. Maintain strict sleep schedule.

rs5751876.name: 1976C/T
rs5751876.summary: ADORA2A encodes the adenosine A2A receptor — caffeine's primary target. The TT genotype is associated with heightened caffeine sensitivity, more caffeine-induced anxiety, and greater sleep disruption from caffeine.
rs5751876.recommendation: TT genotype: caffeine is likely more disruptive to your sleep and may cause more anxiety. Cut caffeine by noon. Consider limiting to 1 cup/day. Decaf after 10am. CT: moderate sensitivity. CC: typically less caffeine-sensitive.

cross_references.implication: ADORA2A (adenosine A2A receptor) rs5751876 T allele is associated with caffeine-induced anxiety. T/T carriers have stronger anxiety response to coffee and may benefit from limiting caffeine. T/T individuals with anxiety: limit caffeine to <100 mg/day or eliminate. Switch to decaf or herbal teas. L-theanine 200 mg can blunt caffeine anxiety in those who continue coffee.

rs1805007.name: R151C
rs1805007.summary: MC1R R151C is a major 'red hair color' variant that disrupts pheomelanin/eumelanin balance. Strongly associated with red/fair hair, freckles, poor tanning, UV sensitivity, and 2–3x increased melanoma risk.
rs1805007.recommendation: Use broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen daily year-round. Avoid tanning beds (strongly associated with melanoma in MC1R variants). Annual full-body skin check by a dermatologist. Wide-brimmed hats and UV-protective clothing. Perform regular self-skin-exams.

cross_references.implication: MC1R R151C (T allele) is essentially absent in non-European populations but reaches significant frequencies in Northern and Western Europe. It is the most common 'red hair' allele. A useful European-ancestry-informative marker.

rs1805008.name: R160W
rs1805008.summary: MC1R R160W is a second major red hair/melanoma risk variant. Carriers have reduced UV protection from melanin and elevated melanoma risk. MC1R variants are among the most common high-penetrance melanoma risk factors.
rs1805008.recommendation: Same as MC1R R151C: daily SPF 50+, annual dermatology check, avoid tanning beds, protective clothing. Effect is cumulative if carrying multiple MC1R variants.

rs1805009.name: D294H
rs1805009.summary: MC1R D294H: third major MC1R variant associated with red/fair phenotype and elevated melanoma risk. Even without red hair, MC1R variant carriers have significantly increased UV sensitivity.
rs1805009.recommendation: Same rigorous photoprotection as other MC1R variants. Melanoma risk is dose-dependent on UV exposure — cumulative sun protection throughout life matters.

rs1110400.name: I155T
rs1110400.summary: MC1R I155T is a moderate-penetrance variant with red hair and melanoma associations. Effect is milder than R151C/R160W/D294H but still confers meaningful UV sensitivity increase.
rs1110400.recommendation: SPF 50+ year-round. Annual dermatology screening. Avoid peak UV hours (10am–4pm). Vitamin D supplementation to compensate for reduced sun exposure.

rs12913832.name: rs12913832 (eye color)
rs12913832.summary: HERC2 rs12913832 is the primary genetic determinant of blue vs. brown eyes. The A allele (blue eyes) is associated with reduced OCA2 expression and lower melanin in the iris. Blue eyes have higher sensitivity to UV damage.
rs12913832.recommendation: Blue-eyed individuals: UV-protective sunglasses are especially important. Wear UV-blocking sunglasses outdoors.

cross_references.implication: HERC2 rs12913832 is the strongest single determinant of blue vs brown eye color. The G allele (associated with blue eyes) is at very high frequency in Northern/Eastern European populations, much lower elsewhere — making it a useful European-ancestry-informative marker.

rs1042602.name: Ser192Tyr
rs1042602.summary: TYR Ser192Tyr affects tyrosinase activity (the key melanin synthesis enzyme), contributing to skin and eye color and UV sensitivity. Associated with melanoma risk, particularly in combination with MC1R variants.
rs1042602.recommendation: Photoprotection particularly important if combined with MC1R variants. Dermatology monitoring.

cross_references.implication: TYR rs1042602 A allele is part of European pigmentation lightening; geographically informative with much higher frequency in Europeans than in non-European populations.

rs1393350.name: Arg402Gln
rs1393350.summary: TYR Arg402Gln reduces tyrosinase enzyme activity by ~40%, contributing to reduced pigmentation and increased UV sensitivity. Associated with oculocutaneous albinism type I in homozygotes.
rs1393350.recommendation: SPF protection as recommended for fair skin. Annual dermatology check if combined with MC1R variants.

rs2981582.name: rs2981582 (breast cancer risk)
rs2981582.summary: FGFR2 rs2981582 is one of the most replicated breast cancer GWAS variants. The A allele increases breast cancer risk ~1.2x per allele. Effect is modest individually but informative in polygenic risk context.
rs2981582.recommendation: Maintain mammography screening per guidelines. Healthy weight (adipose tissue is an estrogen source). Moderate alcohol intake (strong breast cancer risk factor). Regular exercise. Breastfeeding is protective.

rs1219648.name: rs1219648 (breast cancer risk)
rs1219648.summary: Second FGFR2 variant associated with breast cancer risk. Combined with rs2981582 for a fuller FGFR2 risk assessment.
rs1219648.recommendation: Same as rs2981582 — screening, lifestyle modifications, moderate alcohol.

rs80357906.name: 5382insC
rs80357906.summary: BRCA1 5382insC is a founder mutation common in Ashkenazi Jewish and Eastern European populations. Carriers have 60–85% lifetime breast cancer risk and 15–40% ovarian cancer risk.
rs80357906.recommendation: CRITICAL: If positive for this variant, genetic counseling is ESSENTIAL. Discuss with oncologist and genetic counselor: enhanced screening (MRI), chemoprevention, or prophylactic surgery options. Cascade testing for family members. This is a high-penetrance mutation requiring medical management.

rs28897743.name: 6174delT
rs28897743.summary: BRCA2 6174delT is a founder mutation in Ashkenazi Jewish populations. Carriers have ~45–85% lifetime breast cancer risk, 10–20% ovarian cancer risk, and elevated pancreatic and prostate cancer risk in males.
rs28897743.recommendation: CRITICAL: Immediate genetic counseling recommended. Clinical-grade BRCA testing at an accredited lab should follow any positive finding here. Medical management options include enhanced surveillance, chemoprevention, and prophylactic surgery.

rs1042522.name: Pro72Arg
rs1042522.summary: TP53 Pro72Arg affects p53's ability to trigger apoptosis vs. cell-cycle arrest in response to DNA damage. The Arg allele (G) is more efficient at inducing apoptosis but may also increase cancer risk in some genetic backgrounds.
rs1042522.recommendation: TP53 is the most common tumor suppressor mutated in cancer. Protective measures: avoid carcinogens (smoking, excessive UV, aflatoxins), maintain healthy immune function, regular cancer screening appropriate to age and risk.

rs1801155.name: I1307K
rs1801155.summary: APC I1307K is a founder mutation in Ashkenazi Jewish populations (~6% carrier rate). Increases colorectal cancer risk ~1.5–2x by creating a hypermutable region in the APC gene.
rs1801155.recommendation: Earlier and more frequent colorectal cancer screening — colonoscopy starting at age 40 (or earlier) rather than 45–50. Discuss with gastroenterologist. High-fiber diet and regular exercise reduce colorectal cancer risk significantly.

rs17879961.name: I157T
rs17879961.summary: CHEK2 I157T is a moderate-penetrance breast cancer susceptibility variant (~1.5–2x risk). CHEK2 is a DNA damage checkpoint kinase — variants impair cell-cycle arrest after DNA damage.
rs17879961.recommendation: Enhanced breast cancer screening (annual MRI alongside mammography). Genetic counseling recommended. Moderate alcohol intake. Healthy weight. Discuss with oncologist.

rs28897696.name: 1100delC
rs28897696.summary: CHEK2 1100delC is a higher-penetrance breast cancer variant (2–5x risk) common in Northern European populations. Also associated with colorectal, prostate, and thyroid cancer risk.
rs28897696.recommendation: Genetic counseling strongly recommended. Enhanced breast cancer screening protocols. Discuss comprehensive cancer surveillance with an oncologist.

rs3803662.name: rs3803662 (breast cancer risk)
rs3803662.summary: TOX3 rs3803662 is one of the most significant common breast cancer GWAS loci (~1.2x risk per T allele). TOX3 regulates chromatin remodeling and may affect BRCA1 pathway function.
rs3803662.recommendation: Standard breast cancer screening. Lifestyle risk reduction: healthy weight, moderate alcohol, regular exercise, breastfeeding if applicable.

rs6983267.name: rs6983267 (colorectal cancer risk)
rs6983267.summary: The 8q24 region contains enhancers for the MYC oncogene. rs6983267 G allele is significantly associated with colorectal cancer risk (~1.2–1.3x per allele) and also bladder and prostate cancer.
rs6983267.recommendation: Regular colorectal cancer screening (colonoscopy). High-fiber diet, regular physical activity, and maintaining healthy weight all reduce colorectal cancer risk. Avoid excess processed/red meat. Limit alcohol.

rs4939827.name: rs4939827 (colorectal cancer risk)
rs4939827.summary: SMAD7 rs4939827 affects TGF-beta signaling. The T allele is associated with ~1.2x increased colorectal cancer risk. SMAD7 modulates pro-apoptotic signaling in intestinal cells.
rs4939827.recommendation: Regular colorectal screening per cancer-risk guidelines. Anti-inflammatory diet, fiber, and exercise protective.

rs1061170.name: Y402H
rs1061170.summary: CFH Y402H is the strongest genetic risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The T allele (homozygous TT: ~7x risk; heterozygous: ~2.5x) impairs complement regulation in the retina, allowing chronic inflammation.
rs1061170.recommendation: Annual dilated eye exams by an ophthalmologist. Lutein and zeaxanthin supplements (10mg/2mg daily) shown to reduce AMD progression. High-dose AREDS2 formula if intermediate AMD diagnosed. Omega-3 fatty acids. No smoking (dramatically amplifies AMD risk). UV-protective sunglasses.

rs10490924.name: A69S
rs10490924.summary: ARMS2 A69S is the second strongest AMD genetic risk factor. TT genotype confers ~6–8x AMD risk. Combined with CFH Y402H, risks are multiplicative. ARMS2 may be involved in mitochondrial function in photoreceptors.
rs10490924.recommendation: Same as CFH Y402H recommendations. If carrying both CFH and ARMS2 risk variants, proactive ophthalmology care is particularly important. AREDS2 supplementation, lutein/zeaxanthin, omega-3, no smoking.

rs943080.name: rs943080 (AMD/neovascular risk)
rs943080.summary: VEGFA rs943080 is associated with neovascular (wet) AMD risk. Higher VEGF expression promotes abnormal blood vessel growth under the retina. Also relevant for diabetic retinopathy.
rs943080.recommendation: Regular ophthalmology monitoring. VEGF inhibitor injections (anti-VEGF therapy) are highly effective for wet AMD — early treatment is critical to preserve vision.

rs2284665.name: rs2284665 (AMD complement)
rs2284665.summary: CFI (complement factor I) variants affect complement pathway regulation in the retina. Reduced CFI activity allows unchecked complement activation contributing to AMD drusen formation.
rs2284665.recommendation: Ophthalmology monitoring for AMD. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Combined with CFH and ARMS2 for comprehensive AMD risk assessment.

rs2066844.name: R702W
rs2066844.summary: NOD2 R702W is one of three major Crohn's disease variants. NOD2 encodes an innate immune pattern recognition receptor for bacterial muramyl dipeptide. Carriers have 2–4x increased Crohn's risk; compound heterozygotes/homozygotes up to 40x.
rs2066844.recommendation: If experiencing chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, or weight loss: discuss Crohn's disease screening with gastroenterologist (colonoscopy, calprotectin). High-fiber diet when in remission. Avoid smoking (major Crohn's risk factor). Discuss with gastroenterologist.

rs2066845.name: G908R
rs2066845.summary: NOD2 G908R: second major Crohn's disease variant. Combined with other NOD2 variants dramatically increases Crohn's risk and predicts stricturing/penetrating disease behavior.
rs2066845.recommendation: Same as NOD2 R702W. If you carry two NOD2 risk variants, Crohn's disease risk is substantially elevated — proactive gastroenterological evaluation is warranted.

rs5743293.name: 1007fs (frameshift)
rs5743293.summary: NOD2 1007fs (Leu1007fsX1008) is the most common and strongest Crohn's disease variant in Europeans. Frameshifts effectively abolish NOD2 function.
rs5743293.recommendation: Same as other NOD2 variants. This is the most penetrant Crohn's variant — gastroenterological evaluation is warranted if you are a carrier, particularly with GI symptoms.

rs2066827.name: intron 7 L162V proxy
rs2066827.summary: PPARA L162V affects peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha, the key transcription factor for fatty acid beta-oxidation in muscle and liver. Variant associated with altered lipid profile and exercise response.
rs2066827.recommendation: Endurance exercise is particularly valuable for optimizing fatty acid metabolism. Omega-3 fatty acids are PPARA agonists. Fasting periods may help activate PPARA-dependent fat burning.

rs838133.name: rs838133
rs838133.summary: FGF21 variant associated with sweet and alcohol preference. The A allele is linked to higher sugar and alcohol intake via FGF21's role in signaling carbohydrate-induced reward.
rs838133.recommendation: Be mindful of sweet food and alcohol intake. Limit added sugars. FGF21 is induced by fasting and protein restriction — intermittent fasting supports healthy FGF21 signaling.

rs10811661.name: rs10811661 (T2D risk)
rs10811661.summary: CDKN2A/B locus variant associated with reduced pancreatic beta cell mass and increased T2D risk (~1.2x per allele). The T allele impairs beta cell regeneration.
rs10811661.recommendation: Standard T2D prevention: healthy weight, low-glycemic diet, 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise per week, regular glucose monitoring.

rs4977574.name: rs4977574 (CAD risk)
rs4977574.summary: CDKN2B-AS1 rs4977574 (9p21 locus) is the most consistently replicated coronary artery disease GWAS locus, increasing CAD risk ~30% per G allele, independent of cholesterol, blood pressure, or diabetes.
rs4977574.recommendation: Aggressive cardiovascular risk factor control: blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, glucose, smoking cessation, regular aerobic exercise. The 9p21 risk may be partially offset by a Mediterranean diet (multiple studies show dietary modulation of this locus).

rs11206510.name: rs11206510
rs11206510.summary: PCSK9 rs11206510 T allele is associated with higher LDL cholesterol levels by increasing PCSK9 expression (which degrades LDL receptors). PCSK9 inhibitors are now a major drug class for hypercholesterolemia.
rs11206510.recommendation: Monitor LDL cholesterol. If elevated: lifestyle modification (diet, exercise) first. PCSK9 inhibitor medications (evolocumab, alirocumab) may be particularly relevant if statin-insufficient.

rs2228671.name: rs2228671
rs2228671.summary: LDLR variant associated with LDL receptor function and LDL cholesterol levels. Familial hypercholesterolemia involves severe LDLR mutations — this is a common variant with modest LDL effect.
rs2228671.recommendation: Monitor LDL cholesterol. Dietary modification (reduce saturated fat, increase soluble fiber). Discuss statin therapy with your doctor if LDL is elevated.

rs1800775.name: rs1800775
rs1800775.summary: CETP (cholesteryl ester transfer protein) rs1800775 affects HDL cholesterol levels. The A allele is associated with reduced CETP activity and modestly higher HDL levels.
rs1800775.recommendation: Monitor HDL and LDL balance. Regular aerobic exercise most effectively raises HDL. Moderate alcohol raises HDL but risks outweigh benefits. Niacin and omega-3 also raise HDL.

rs328.name: S447X
rs328.summary: LPL S447X: the X (stop) allele (G) is actually the beneficial variant — associated with higher LPL activity, lower triglycerides, and reduced CAD risk. The C allele (S447) is the more common, less favorable variant.
rs328.recommendation: Triglyceride management: low simple carbohydrate/added sugar diet, regular exercise, moderate alcohol consumption, omega-3 supplementation. Monitor fasting triglycerides.

rs4516035.name: Bsm1 (A/G)
rs4516035.summary: VDR Bsm1 is one of several VDR RFLP variants associated with bone density, cancer susceptibility, and immune function. Effect is modest and context-dependent.
rs4516035.recommendation: Maintain optimal vitamin D levels (25(OH)D 40–60 ng/mL). Adequate calcium intake and weight-bearing exercise for bone health.

rs7975232.name: ApaI (C/A)
rs7975232.summary: VDR ApaI is another common VDR polymorphism affecting vitamin D receptor haplotype. Combined analysis of VDR RFLP variants (BsmI, ApaI, TaqI, FokI) provides a more complete picture of vitamin D receptor function.
rs7975232.recommendation: Optimize vitamin D levels. Combine with FokI and TaqI for comprehensive VDR haplotype assessment.

rs1800468.name: T869C (L10P)
rs1800468.summary: TGFB1 L10P affects TGF-beta1 secretion levels. TGF-beta is a pleiotropic cytokine that regulates immune responses, wound healing, and fibrosis. High TGF-beta is associated with fibrotic disease; low with autoimmune risk.
rs1800468.recommendation: No specific action needed alone. Relevant context in fibrotic conditions (pulmonary fibrosis, cardiac fibrosis) — discuss with doctor if relevant family history.

rs1137101.name: Q223R
rs1137101.summary: LEPR Q223R affects the leptin receptor, which mediates satiety signaling from fat cells to the hypothalamus. The A allele is associated with leptin resistance, higher BMI, and increased obesity risk.
rs1137101.recommendation: High-protein diet improves leptin sensitivity. Regular exercise restores leptin signaling. Adequate sleep is critical (sleep deprivation dramatically worsens leptin resistance). Avoid high-fructose corn syrup (directly causes leptin resistance).

rs2302429.name: rs2302429
rs2302429.summary: GH1 (growth hormone) variant associated with IGF-1 axis function, affecting muscle development, fat metabolism, and recovery from exercise.
rs2302429.recommendation: Optimize sleep quality (80% of growth hormone is released during deep sleep). Resistance training stimulates GH release. Intermittent fasting enhances GH secretion.

rs6313.name: T102C
rs6313.summary: HTR2A T102C affects serotonin 2A receptor expression. Associated with schizophrenia susceptibility, antidepressant (SSRI) response, and eating disorder risk in some populations.
rs6313.recommendation: Discuss SSRI response with psychiatrist — this variant may predict antipsychotic and antidepressant response. Inform prescribers.

rs2304672.name: rs2304672
rs2304672.summary: PER3 rs2304672 contributes to circadian period length and chronotype. Associated with delayed sleep phase and evening preference.
rs2304672.recommendation: Consistent sleep schedule, morning bright light exposure to advance circadian phase. Avoid late-night bright light.

rs10757274.name: rs10757274 (CAD risk)
rs10757274.summary: Second 9p21 locus variant strongly associated with coronary artery disease. The G allele increases CAD, stroke, and abdominal aortic aneurysm risk. Independent of classical cardiovascular risk factors.
rs10757274.recommendation: Rigorous cardiovascular risk management. Mediterranean diet particularly attenuates this locus. Regular aerobic exercise, blood pressure control, no smoking.

rs1800734.name: MLH1 promoter (-93G/A)
rs1800734.summary: MLH1 promoter variant associated with Lynch syndrome and colorectal cancer susceptibility. MLH1 is a mismatch repair gene — reduced expression causes microsatellite instability.
rs1800734.recommendation: Discuss Lynch syndrome evaluation with a genetic counselor if family history of colorectal, endometrial, or ovarian cancer. Regular colonoscopy screening per Lynch syndrome guidelines if confirmed.

rs4343.name: I/D proxy (rs4343)
rs4343.summary: ACE rs4343 (D-allele proxy) is associated with higher ACE enzyme activity, elevated angiotensin II, and increased blood pressure and left ventricular hypertrophy risk. D allele is a risk factor for cardiovascular and renal disease.
rs4343.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure regularly. Low-sodium diet. Regular aerobic exercise. ACE inhibitors may be particularly effective for this genotype — discuss with your cardiologist.

rs693.name: rs693 (ApoB level)
rs693.summary: APOB rs693 is associated with ApoB lipoprotein levels and LDL particle count. Elevated ApoB is a cardiovascular risk factor independent of LDL cholesterol.
rs693.recommendation: Request ApoB testing alongside standard lipid panel. Statins and dietary changes reduce ApoB. Mediterranean diet with limited saturated fat.

rs1333049.name: rs1333049 (9p21 CAD locus)
rs1333049.summary: 9p21 CAD locus rs1333049 C allele is one of the most replicated coronary artery disease risk variants, increasing CAD risk ~30% independent of classical risk factors.
rs1333049.recommendation: Aggressive cardiovascular risk factor management. Mediterranean diet may specifically attenuate 9p21 risk (shown in PREDIMED trial). Regular aerobic exercise and no smoking.

rs2036914.name: rs2036914 (Factor XI)
rs2036914.summary: Factor XI rs2036914 influences circulating Factor XI levels and modestly affects venous thromboembolism risk. Factor XI plays a role in the amplification phase of coagulation.
rs2036914.recommendation: Standard thrombosis prevention measures. Relevant context if combined with Factor V Leiden or prothrombin variants.

rs4778138.name: rs4778138 (melanin/skin)
rs4778138.summary: OCA2 rs4778138 contributes to skin and eye pigmentation. Lower pigmentation alleles are associated with higher UV sensitivity and modestly elevated melanoma risk.
rs4778138.recommendation: Fair-skinned individuals: diligent sun protection (SPF 50+), annual dermatology check.

rs1799977.name: Ile219Val
rs1799977.summary: MLH1 Ile219Val is a mismatch repair gene variant associated with modest colorectal cancer risk and Lynch syndrome susceptibility in compound heterozygotes.
rs1799977.recommendation: Standard colorectal cancer screening. If family history of Lynch syndrome cancers exists, discuss genetic counseling.

rs10830963.name: rs10830963 (melatonin receptor)
rs10830963.summary: MTNR1B rs10830963 G allele is associated with elevated fasting glucose and impaired insulin secretion during evening hours when melatonin is elevated. Risk is amplified by late eating habits.
rs10830963.recommendation: Strictly avoid late-night eating. Time-restricted eating with an earlier window (7am-5pm or 8am-6pm) has shown particular benefit in G allele carriers. Monitor fasting glucose.

rs601338.name: W154X (non-secretor)
rs601338.summary: FUT2 non-secretors (AA) cannot secrete blood-type antigens into mucus. This alters gut microbiome composition and is associated with higher norovirus susceptibility, lower gut Bifidobacterium, and reduced B12 absorption.
rs601338.recommendation: Non-secretors may benefit from probiotic supplementation (especially Bifidobacterium strains). Monitor B12 status. Aware of slightly higher norovirus susceptibility.

rs2227564.name: rs2227564
rs2227564.summary: MLH1 rs2227564 is associated with mismatch repair activity and colorectal cancer susceptibility, particularly in combination with other MLH1 variants.
rs2227564.recommendation: Standard colorectal cancer screening. Discuss family history with gastroenterologist.

rs4820268.name: rs4820268
rs4820268.summary: TMPRSS6 rs4820268 is associated with serum ferritin and iron levels. Combined with rs855791, provides a more complete picture of iron absorption regulation.
rs4820268.recommendation: Monitor ferritin and CBC, especially in premenopausal women or with heavy exercise. Ensure adequate dietary iron.

rs3027178.name: rs3027178
rs3027178.summary: PER1 (Period Circadian Regulator 1) rs3027178 contributes to circadian period length and chronotype. Associated with morning chronotype and altered sleep architecture.
rs3027178.recommendation: Consistent sleep and wake times. Light exposure matched to chronotype preference for optimal circadian health.

rs1042026.name: Ile349Val
rs1042026.summary: ADH1C Ile349Val affects alcohol dehydrogenase 1C activity and alcohol metabolism rate. The gamma1 allele (slow) is associated with higher acetaldehyde exposure per drink and modestly altered cancer risk.
rs1042026.recommendation: Moderate alcohol consumption. Combined with ALDH2 and ADH1B for comprehensive alcohol metabolism assessment.

rs2279343.name: *9 (Q172H)
rs2279343.summary: CYP2B6 *9 reduces CYP2B6 activity and contributes to slow efavirenz and bupropion metabolism. Combined with *6 (rs3745274), can create poor metabolizer phenotype.
rs2279343.recommendation: Inform prescribers if on efavirenz, bupropion, or cyclophosphamide. Combined CYP2B6 genotyping determines final metabolizer phenotype.

rs4714.name: C825T
rs4714.summary: GNB3 C825T affects G-protein beta3 subunit signaling in vascular and adipose tissue. The T allele is associated with hypertension, obesity, and altered antidepressant response.
rs4714.recommendation: Blood pressure monitoring. Low-sodium diet. GNB3 variant may predict antidepressant response — discuss with psychiatrist if relevant.

rs5186.name: A1166C
rs5186.summary: AGTR1 A1166C affects angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression. The C allele is associated with increased vascular responsiveness to angiotensin II, higher blood pressure, and hypertensive response to dietary salt.
rs5186.recommendation: Low-sodium diet is particularly important. Regular blood pressure monitoring. ARB medications (losartan, valsartan) directly target this receptor pathway.

rs10954213.name: rs10954213
rs10954213.summary: IRF5 rs10954213 (A allele) is associated with increased IRF5 expression and elevated risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease.
rs10954213.recommendation: Discuss autoimmune screening with doctor if experiencing joint pain, fatigue, rash, or other symptoms. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle and adequate vitamin D are protective.

rs3918242.name: C1562T
rs3918242.summary: MMP9 C1562T increases matrix metalloproteinase-9 expression, which degrades extracellular matrix in atherosclerotic plaques, potentially destabilizing them. Associated with increased risk of plaque rupture and acute coronary events.
rs3918242.recommendation: Optimize cardiovascular risk factors. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle (Mediterranean diet, exercise). Omega-3 fatty acids reduce MMP9 activity.

rs2071348.name: rs2071348 (Hepcidin)
rs2071348.summary: HAMP encodes hepcidin, the master regulator of iron absorption. Variants affecting hepcidin expression can alter iron homeostasis and contribute to iron overload or deficiency.
rs2071348.recommendation: Monitor serum ferritin and transferrin saturation. Relevant context alongside HFE and TMPRSS6 variants for full iron metabolism picture.

rs6311.name: A-1438G
rs6311.summary: HTR2A A-1438G promoter variant affects serotonin 2A receptor expression and is associated with depression susceptibility and differential response to SSRIs and antipsychotics.
rs6311.recommendation: Inform psychiatrist — HTR2A variants can predict antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment response. Consider pharmacogenomic testing before psychiatric medication selection.

rs61750900.name: 167delT
rs61750900.summary: GJB2 167delT is the most common hearing-loss mutation in Ashkenazi Jewish populations (carrier rate ~4%). Homozygotes or compound heterozygotes with other GJB2 variants develop sensorineural hearing loss.
rs61750900.recommendation: Carrier: consider genetic counseling before family planning. Audiological evaluation if hearing difficulties present. Cochlear implants are highly effective for GJB2-related hearing loss.

rs6152.name: Androgen Receptor (rs6152, CAG-repeat proxy)
rs6152.summary: AR rs6152 is a synonymous variant adjacent to the AR CAG-repeat tract. Although it does not itself change the protein, it serves as a partial proxy for CAG-repeat length, which inversely correlates with androgen receptor sensitivity. Shorter CAG tracts → more transcriptional response per molecule of testosterone (more sensitive); longer tracts → less sensitive (relatively higher T may be needed for the same effect).
rs6152.recommendation: If experiencing low-T-like symptoms despite normal total testosterone, ask your doctor about free T, SHBG, and a sensitivity-aware interpretation. Strength training, adequate sleep (7–9 h), zinc/vitamin D sufficiency, and minimizing chronic alcohol all support androgen signaling regardless of receptor sensitivity.

rs523349.name: V89L (rs523349)
rs523349.summary: SRD5A2 V89L (C allele = L variant) reduces 5-alpha reductase type 2 activity by 30–40%. This enzyme converts testosterone to DHT, the more potent androgen driving prostate growth, scalp hair-follicle miniaturization, beard density, and body hair. Lower activity → less DHT → relatively lower risk of androgenetic alopecia and BPH, but may slightly attenuate masculinizing effects.
rs523349.recommendation: Carriers of the slow allele who use testosterone-elevating strategies will see relatively less DHT-mediated effect. If concerned about hair loss in a fast variant: avoid unnecessary supraphysiologic T; saw palmetto and pumpkin seed oil are weak natural 5-AR inhibitors. Discuss finasteride/dutasteride with a doctor only if clinically indicated.

rs6259.name: D356N (rs6259)
rs6259.summary: SHBG rs6259 (A allele = N variant) increases circulating SHBG by ~10–20%, lowering bioavailable (free) testosterone for a given total T. People with higher SHBG often report low-T symptoms despite normal total T on labs.
rs6259.recommendation: If symptomatic, ensure your panel includes free T and SHBG, not just total T. Strategies to lower SHBG: adequate protein and carbohydrate intake (very low-carb diets raise SHBG), boron supplementation (3–10 mg/day has modest evidence), magnesium sufficiency, healthy body composition, and resistance training.

rs1799941.name: rs1799941 (5'-flanking)
rs1799941.summary: SHBG rs1799941 is a promoter variant; the A allele is associated with higher SHBG levels and lower free testosterone. It also modestly increases SHBG response to estrogen and thyroid stimulation. Combined effect with rs6259 can be additive for elevated SHBG.
