rs1799941.recommendation: See rs6259 strategies. People with both rs1799941 A and rs6259 A should pay particular attention to SHBG-lowering lifestyle levers (adequate calorie intake, boron, magnesium, body composition).

rs12150660.name: rs12150660
rs12150660.summary: rs12150660 is a SHBG-locus variant from large GWAS of circulating SHBG and free androgen index (FAI). The T allele is associated with higher SHBG and correspondingly lower FAI in men.
rs12150660.recommendation: Combine SHBG-related variants for an overall picture of bioavailable T. If symptomatic, request a free T / SHBG / total T panel. Lifestyle strategies overlap with rs6259.

rs4646.name: rs4646 (aromatase 3'-UTR)
rs4646.summary: CYP19A1 encodes aromatase, which converts testosterone to estradiol. The A allele of rs4646 is associated with somewhat reduced aromatase activity and a higher testosterone-to-estradiol (T:E2) ratio. This is generally favorable for masculinizing effects but can mean lower estrogen, which is itself needed for bone, cognition, libido, and cardiovascular health.
rs4646.recommendation: Do not assume 'less estrogen is better.' Optimal T:E2 in men is roughly 10–30:1 by mass; chronically low E2 (<20 pg/mL) is associated with low libido, depression, bone loss. Resistance training, healthy body fat (15–20%), and avoiding excessive alcohol all help. Do not self-administer aromatase inhibitors without medical supervision.

rs10046.name: rs10046
rs10046.summary: CYP19A1 rs10046 affects aromatase expression. The T allele is generally associated with higher aromatase activity and lower T:E2 ratio in men (more conversion of T to estrogen) — sometimes contributing to gynecomastia susceptibility or estrogen-dominant symptoms in men with higher body fat.
rs10046.recommendation: Body fat is a major modifier — adipose tissue is the primary site of aromatization in men. Maintaining lean body composition (≤20% body fat) is the most reliable lever. Zinc, DIM (from cruciferous vegetables), and limiting alcohol modestly support healthier T:E2. Discuss with a doctor before any pharmacologic intervention.

rs2234693.name: PvuII (rs2234693)
rs2234693.summary: ESR1 (estrogen receptor alpha) rs2234693: the C allele is associated with somewhat greater estrogen sensitivity and is linked to better bone density response to estrogen, but also relevance for cardiovascular and reproductive phenotypes. Combined with rs9340799, it defines common ESR1 haplotypes affecting estrogen signaling.
rs2234693.recommendation: Bone density support: adequate vitamin D, calcium, weight-bearing exercise. In men, do not aggressively suppress estradiol — it is essential for bone, libido, and cognitive function. Cross-references include male fertility (estrogen signaling in spermatogenesis).

cross_references.implication: ESR1 (estrogen receptor alpha) is required for normal spermatogenesis — estrogen signalling in the testis modulates Sertoli-cell function. Polymorphisms affecting estrogen sensitivity have been associated with sperm parameters in some studies. Do not aggressively suppress estradiol — modest E2 is needed for fertility.

rs9340799.name: XbaI (rs9340799)
rs9340799.summary: ESR1 rs9340799 is the second classic ESR1 promoter SNP. The G allele forms part of the 'PX' haplotype (with rs2234693 C) and modifies estrogen-dependent gene expression. Associations include bone mineral density, cardiovascular events, and reproductive phenotypes.
rs9340799.recommendation: See rs2234693. Interpret PvuII + XbaI as a haplotype where possible. Lifestyle support: weight-bearing exercise, adequate D/K2/calcium, healthy body composition.

rs7436962.name: rs7436962 (UGT2B17 deletion proxy)
rs7436962.summary: The UGT2B17 gene has a copy-number deletion (CNV) that is the dominant determinant of urinary testosterone glucuronide excretion and is used in anti-doping interpretation. rs7436962 is one of several SNPs reported as partial proxies for deletion status. Deletion carriers excrete much less testosterone in urine (5–10× lower) and may have modestly different testosterone metabolism — though serum T levels are mostly unaffected.
rs7436962.recommendation: Mostly relevant for anti-doping interpretation (T/E ratio in WADA testing). For health, this variant is not strongly actionable. Standard hormone-optimization advice (sleep, training, protein, zinc, vitamin D) applies.

rs2066479.name: rs2066479
rs2066479.summary: HSD17B3 (17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3) is the testicular enzyme that converts androstenedione to testosterone. Rare loss-of-function mutations cause 46,XY DSD. Common variants like rs2066479 are associated with modest differences in T synthesis and circulating androgens.
rs2066479.recommendation: Effect size is modest. Standard T-supportive lifestyle (avoiding chronic energy deficit, sleep, resistance training, vitamin D, zinc) applies.

rs6166.name: Asn680Ser (rs6166)
rs6166.summary: FSHR rs6166 (G allele = Ser variant) modestly reduces FSH receptor sensitivity. In men this can mean slightly higher circulating FSH for the same Sertoli-cell stimulus and modest effects on spermatogenesis; in women it is associated with response to FSH stimulation in fertility treatment.
rs6166.recommendation: Mostly relevant if hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal evaluation is being done for fertility. Standard fertility lifestyle (avoid heat, alcohol, smoking; ensure zinc, selenium, folate) applies.

rs2845570.name: rs2845570
rs2845570.summary: CATSPER1 encodes a sperm-specific calcium channel essential for hyperactivated motility and the ability of sperm to penetrate the egg's zona pellucida. Common variants such as rs2845570 are associated with subtle differences in motility parameters; severe loss-of-function causes male infertility.
rs2845570.recommendation: Calcium signalling depends on overall sperm health. Support motility with adequate zinc, CoQ10 (200 mg/day), L-carnitine (1–2 g/day), omega-3s, and avoidance of scrotal heat (long hot tubs, laptops on lap, tight underwear).

rs1045945.name: rs1045945
rs1045945.summary: DAZL (Deleted in Azoospermia-Like) is required for germ cell development. Common SNPs such as rs1045945 are associated with modest reductions in sperm count and azoospermia risk in some populations; large Y-chromosome AZF deletions (separate from this SNP) cause more severe phenotypes.
rs1045945.recommendation: If trying to conceive and a semen analysis shows low count, ask about a urology referral and Y-chromosome AZFa/b/c testing. Folate, zinc, and antioxidants support spermatogenesis; avoid chronic high heat and excess alcohol.

rs4796909.name: rs4796909
rs4796909.summary: USP26 is an X-linked deubiquitinating enzyme highly expressed in testis, where it regulates protein turnover during spermatogenesis. Variants including rs4796909 have been associated with altered spermatogenic phenotypes in some studies, though effect sizes are modest and reproducibility varies.
rs4796909.recommendation: Standard male fertility optimization: avoid testicular heat, ensure 7–9 h sleep, moderate exercise, no smoking, limit alcohol, supplement zinc 25 mg/day and selenium 100–200 µg/day if dietary intake is low.

rs1050450.name: Pro198Leu (rs1050450)
rs1050450.summary: GPX1 (glutathione peroxidase 1) is a selenium-dependent antioxidant that protects cells — including sperm — from oxidative damage. The T allele (Leu variant) modestly reduces enzymatic activity, increasing vulnerability to oxidative stress in sperm DNA, mitochondria, and membranes. Also relevant for cancer risk and heavy-metal detoxification.
rs1050450.recommendation: Ensure adequate selenium (100–200 µg/day; Brazil nuts are exceptionally rich). Combine with other antioxidants (CoQ10, vitamin C 500 mg/day, vitamin E 200 IU/day, NAC 600 mg twice/day) particularly when trying to conceive. Also relevant for fluoride/mercury exposure tolerance.

cross_references.implication: GPX1 detoxifies mercury, lead-induced peroxides, and selenium-dependent antioxidant defense more broadly. Pro198Leu T allele reduces capacity. Maintain selenium 100–200 µg/day (Brazil nuts, fish, eggs). Combine with NAC, vitamin C/E for broader antioxidant support.

rs1065852.name: *10 (P34S, rs1065852)
rs1065852.summary: CYP2D6 rs1065852 (A allele) tags the *10 reduced-function allele, common in East Asian populations and contributing to intermediate-metabolizer status. CYP2D6 metabolizes many psychiatric medications (atomoxetine, some antidepressants, some opioids). Reduced function can lead to higher drug exposure and side effects at standard doses.
rs1065852.recommendation: Critical for atomoxetine (Strattera) dosing — poor/intermediate metabolizers may need lower doses or different drugs. Inform any prescribing psychiatrist of CYP2D6 status. Avoid combining CYP2D6 substrates with strong inhibitors (paroxetine, bupropion, fluoxetine). DO NOT change medications based on this alone — discuss with a prescriber.

rs16947.name: *2 (rs16947)
rs16947.summary: CYP2D6 rs16947 is a common SNP defining the *2 family of alleles (mostly normal-function but variable). Combined with other CYP2D6 SNPs it helps define the overall metabolizer phenotype (poor/intermediate/normal/rapid/ultra-rapid).
rs16947.recommendation: On its own, rs16947 is not strongly actionable — CYP2D6 phenotype requires the combination of multiple variants and copy-number assessment. For psychiatric medications, ask your prescriber whether formal CYP2D6 pharmacogenomic testing is warranted.

rs1135840.name: S486T (rs1135840)
rs1135840.summary: CYP2D6 rs1135840 is part of several star-allele haplotypes including *2 and *4. Helps refine CYP2D6 phenotype prediction when combined with rs3892097 and rs1065852.
rs1135840.recommendation: See rs3892097 / rs1065852. CYP2D6 phenotype is a haplotype, not a single SNP — formal pharmacogenomic testing is the gold standard for medication decisions.

rs2740574.name: *1B (rs2740574)
rs2740574.summary: CYP3A4 is the most prolific drug-metabolizing enzyme — metabolizes ~50% of all clinically used drugs. rs2740574 (*1B, G allele) is a promoter variant associated with altered expression in some studies, with population-specific frequency (common in African ancestry, rare in Europeans).
rs2740574.recommendation: CYP3A4 activity varies enormously with diet (grapefruit, St. John's Wort) and co-medications. For medications with narrow therapeutic indices (tacrolimus, some statins, midazolam), avoid grapefruit juice and inform prescribers of any new medications.

rs27072.name: rs27072
rs27072.summary: SLC6A3 (DAT1) encodes the dopamine transporter — the primary target of amphetamines (Vyvanse, Adderall) and methylphenidate (Ritalin, Concerta). rs27072 is associated with DAT1 expression and ADHD treatment response. The 10R/10R VNTR genotype (often correlated with this SNP) has been associated with less robust response to methylphenidate in some studies.
rs27072.recommendation: Pharmacogenomic studies have mixed results — single SNPs are weak predictors of stimulant response. Genetic context is only one input; psychiatric assessment and clinical titration remain primary. STRONG DISCLAIMER: Medication decisions, including which stimulant to try, must involve a psychiatrist.

rs2652511.name: rs2652511
rs2652511.summary: SLC6A3 rs2652511 is another DAT1-locus variant studied for ADHD susceptibility and stimulant response. Associations are heterogeneous across studies.
rs2652511.recommendation: See rs27072. The genetics of ADHD medication response are complex and polygenic. Use this information as background context for conversations with your psychiatrist, not as a decision rule.

rs1800544.name: -1291 C/G (rs1800544)
rs1800544.summary: ADRA2A (alpha-2A adrenergic receptor) is a target of guanfacine and clonidine, and the receptor modulates prefrontal cortex norepinephrine signalling. rs1800544 has been associated with attention performance and methylphenidate response — in some studies G-allele carriers show larger improvements in attention.
rs1800544.recommendation: Particularly relevant if considering guanfacine (Intuniv) or clonidine for ADHD. Combine with sleep, exercise, and CBT-style attention strategies. Medication decisions belong with a psychiatrist.

rs36017.name: rs36017 (NET)
rs36017.summary: SLC6A2 encodes the norepinephrine transporter (NET), a key target of atomoxetine (Strattera), Vyvanse's NE component, and many tricyclic antidepressants. rs36017 has been studied for response to NET-targeting drugs with mixed results.
rs36017.recommendation: Single SNP effects are small. If considering atomoxetine, monitor with structured rating scales (ASRS, Conners). Discuss with prescriber.

rs363050.name: rs363050
rs363050.summary: SNAP25 is a presynaptic protein essential for neurotransmitter release. Variants including rs363050 have been associated with ADHD susceptibility and methylphenidate response in pediatric populations.
rs363050.recommendation: Effect size is modest. ADHD is highly polygenic — no single variant determines clinical course or response to medication. Pair any psychiatric medication trial with structured outcome measurement.

rs6551665.name: rs6551665
rs6551665.summary: LPHN3 (latrophilin-3, now ADGRL3) is one of the more replicated ADHD susceptibility genes. rs6551665 G allele is associated with increased ADHD risk in multiple populations and with response to stimulant medication.
rs6551665.recommendation: Background ADHD-risk context only — not a diagnostic marker. ADHD diagnosis is clinical (DSM-5 criteria, functional impairment). If diagnosed, evidence-based treatment includes stimulants, atomoxetine, behavioral therapy, sleep optimization, and exercise.

rs71748309.name: rs71748309 (GSTT1 deletion proxy)
rs71748309.summary: GSTT1 is a glutathione S-transferase that conjugates many environmental electrophiles (some halogenated hydrocarbons, ethylene oxide). The gene has a common whole-gene deletion polymorphism — homozygous deletion (~20% of Europeans, ~40% of East Asians) abolishes activity. rs71748309 is one of several tag SNPs used to infer deletion status, though direct CNV assays are more reliable.
rs71748309.recommendation: If you suspect functional deletion: increase glutathione precursors — N-acetylcysteine (NAC) 600 mg twice/day, sulforaphane (broccoli sprouts), whey protein. Minimize chlorinated solvent exposure (dry-cleaned clothes, paint thinners). Filter drinking water for chlorinated byproducts.

rs366631.name: rs366631 (GSTM1 deletion proxy)
rs366631.summary: GSTM1 is another glutathione S-transferase with a common whole-gene deletion (~50% of Europeans homozygous null). GSTM1-null status is associated with reduced ability to detoxify benzene, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (from cooking fumes, grilled meat, traffic), and mercury/cadmium. rs366631 is a tag SNP proxy.
rs366631.recommendation: Null status moderately increases susceptibility to lung cancer (smokers), bladder cancer (occupational exposures), and heavy-metal accumulation. Reduce exposures: avoid smoking, minimize charred/grilled meat, vent cooking fumes, use HEPA filtration in high-pollution areas. Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, kale, Brussels sprouts) upregulate other detox pathways via Nrf2.

rs8052394.name: rs8052394
rs8052394.summary: Metallothioneins (MT) bind and sequester heavy metals (zinc, copper, cadmium, mercury, arsenic). MT1A rs8052394 affects baseline expression and inducibility. The G allele may be associated with reduced expression and greater vulnerability to cadmium accumulation in some studies.
rs8052394.recommendation: Maintain zinc sufficiency (15–30 mg/day) — zinc is the primary inducer of metallothionein. Avoid cadmium sources (cigarette smoke, some rice grown in cadmium-contaminated soil). Selenium (100–200 µg/day) supports heavy-metal binding and excretion.

rs10636.name: rs10636 (+838 G/C)
rs10636.summary: MT2A rs10636 is a 3'-UTR variant affecting metallothionein 2A expression. Associated in various studies with cadmium body burden, susceptibility to oxidative stress, and gestational diabetes risk.
rs10636.recommendation: Strategy is similar to rs8052394 — zinc adequacy, selenium, glutathione support. Test heavy-metal exposure with provoked or unprovoked urine testing if symptomatic and exposure is plausible.

rs2071746.name: rs2071746 (HMOX1 promoter)
rs2071746.summary: HMOX1 (heme oxygenase 1) is a master antioxidant and anti-inflammatory enzyme, induced by oxidative and metal stress. The promoter GT-repeat (and associated SNPs like rs2071746) modulates inducibility. Lower-inducibility variants are associated with worse outcomes after oxidative insults including heavy-metal exposure, smoking, and ischemia/reperfusion injury.
rs2071746.recommendation: Support Nrf2 pathway (master regulator of HMOX1): sulforaphane (broccoli sprouts ~10 g/day or supplement), curcumin (500–1000 mg/day with bioperine), green tea EGCG, regular exercise. Reduce oxidative-stress load: stop smoking, treat sleep apnea, manage iron overload if HFE+.

rs4646903.name: MspI (rs4646903)
rs4646903.summary: CYP1A1 activates polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (from smoking, grilled meat, traffic pollution) and some pesticides into reactive carcinogenic intermediates. The C allele of rs4646903 (and the *2A haplotype) is associated with higher inducibility — meaning faster activation of these compounds, which can be problematic when conjugation pathways (GST) are slow.
rs4646903.recommendation: Combination of fast CYP1A1 + slow GSTM1 (null) is particularly disadvantageous — high carcinogen activation, low clearance. Practical mitigation: avoid smoking, minimize charred/grilled meat, eat cruciferous vegetables (induce phase II), HEPA filter in polluted areas.

rs1056836.name: L432V (rs1056836)
rs1056836.summary: CYP1B1 metabolizes estrogens, dioxin, and several environmental carcinogens. The G allele (Val variant) increases catalytic activity, particularly for 4-hydroxylation of estradiol — relevant for estrogen-driven cancers and for activating environmental procarcinogens.
rs1056836.recommendation: Pair with phase II support (broccoli sprouts → sulforaphane → glutathione transferases). Reduce xenobiotic load (alcohol, refined vegetable oils, plastic-stored hot food). For women, this variant has implications for breast cancer risk in combination with COMT slow variants.

rs2066853.name: R554K (rs2066853)
rs2066853.summary: AHR (aryl hydrocarbon receptor) senses dioxins, PCBs, PAHs, and tryptophan metabolites; activated AHR drives transcription of CYP1A1/B1. The A allele (Lys variant) is associated with altered AHR activity and pollutant susceptibility.
rs2066853.recommendation: Minimize dioxin/PCB exposure: limit high-trophic-level fish (large tuna, swordfish), favor wild salmon, sardines, anchovies. Indole-3-carbinol from cruciferous vegetables modulates AHR signalling. Maintain healthy gut microbiome — tryptophan-derived AHR ligands are important for gut barrier.

rs2802292.name: rs2802292
rs2802292.summary: FOXO3 is one of the most replicated longevity genes — the G allele of rs2802292 is enriched in centenarians across multiple ancestries (Japanese, German, Italian, US). FOXO3 mediates cellular stress resistance, autophagy, antioxidant defense, and insulin/IGF-1 signalling.
rs2802292.recommendation: FOXO3 activity is supported by intermittent fasting/time-restricted eating (lower insulin/IGF-1), resistance + aerobic exercise, polyphenols (resveratrol, EGCG, curcumin), and caloric restriction (or its mimetics). G carriers may benefit somewhat more from these interventions but they are good for everyone.

rs5882.name: I405V (rs5882)
rs5882.summary: CETP I405V (A = V variant) is associated with reduced CETP activity, higher HDL cholesterol, larger LDL particle size, and — in some studies — increased exceptional longevity and reduced dementia incidence. Effect on cardiovascular events is complex (large pharmacological CETP inhibition trials had mixed results).
rs5882.recommendation: Generally favourable cholesterol profile. Continue standard cardioprotective lifestyle: Mediterranean diet, regular exercise (both aerobic and resistance), avoid smoking, moderate alcohol. Do not over-rely on a single SNP — full lipid panel + ApoB is the better risk measure.

rs2736100.name: rs2736100
rs2736100.summary: TERT (telomerase reverse transcriptase) rs2736100 C allele is associated with longer telomere length and modestly increased risk of certain cancers (lung adenocarcinoma, glioma) — illustrating the longevity/cancer trade-off in telomere biology. Effect sizes are small.
rs2736100.recommendation: Telomere length is modifiable: regular exercise (aerobic + resistance), Mediterranean-style diet, stress management (meditation has telomerase-supporting evidence), adequate sleep. Avoid smoking. Routine telomere-length testing is not clinically recommended.

rs1360780.name: rs1360780
rs1360780.summary: FKBP5 modulates glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity — affects how cortisol signals are translated into cellular responses. The T allele of rs1360780 is associated with prolonged cortisol response to stress, higher risk of PTSD after trauma, and altered antidepressant response (some studies show better response to certain SSRIs).
rs1360780.recommendation: Prioritize trauma-informed mental health care if history of significant stressors. Daily stress-management practices (meditation, breathwork, regular sleep, exercise) reduce HPA-axis dysregulation. Discuss with a psychiatrist if struggling with mood/anxiety — choice of antidepressant may benefit from FKBP5-aware interpretation.

rs1006737.name: rs1006737
rs1006737.summary: CACNA1C encodes a calcium channel subunit implicated in mood disorders. rs1006737 A allele has been associated in large GWAS with bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and major depression — though effect on any individual is small (OR ~1.1–1.2).
rs1006737.recommendation: Single SNP risk is small and not deterministic. If personal/family history of bipolar disorder or psychosis, watch for warning signs (sleep disruption, racing thoughts, grandiosity, paranoia) and engage psychiatric care early. Regular sleep schedule is particularly protective for those at bipolar risk.

rs53576.name: rs53576
rs53576.summary: OXTR (oxytocin receptor) rs53576 has been associated with social cognition, empathy, social-buffering of stress, and parenting behavior. G/G homozygotes are reported to show somewhat more empathic accuracy and social sensitivity in some studies; A allele carriers may be less reactive to social cues but show no overall pathology. Replication is mixed; effects are small.
rs53576.recommendation: Social connection is one of the strongest predictors of longevity and mental health for everyone. Cultivate close relationships, physical affection, group activities — oxytocin systems respond to behavior.

rs7454108.name: rs7454108 (HLA-DQ8 proxy)
rs7454108.summary: rs7454108 is a tag SNP for the HLA-DQ8 haplotype (DQB1*0302), the second major celiac-risk haplotype after DQ2. ~5% of celiac patients carry DQ8 in the absence of DQ2; the C allele tags DQ8. Together, DQ2 + DQ8 cover ~99% of celiac risk.
rs7454108.recommendation: Combined with rs2187668 (DQ2): essentially all celiac cases occur in carriers. Positive does not mean celiac will develop (only ~3% of carriers develop overt disease) — but if symptoms (GI, fatigue, anemia, neurological), test tTG-IgA with normal gluten intake before going gluten-free. Negative for both DQ2 and DQ8 essentially rules out celiac.

rs4349859.name: rs4349859 (HLA-B*27 proxy)
rs4349859.summary: rs4349859 is a tag SNP for HLA-B*27, strongly associated with ankylosing spondylitis (~90% of AS patients carry B27; ~6–8% of B27 carriers develop AS). Also associated with acute anterior uveitis, reactive arthritis, and some forms of psoriatic arthritis.
rs4349859.recommendation: Being B27+ does not mean AS will develop. If chronic inflammatory back pain (>3 months, age <45, morning stiffness >30 min, alternating buttock pain, improving with exercise), see a rheumatologist for MRI of sacroiliac joints. Regular exercise (especially postural/range-of-motion work, swimming) is foundational. Do not smoke — strongly accelerates AS.

rs61816761.name: R501X (rs61816761)
rs61816761.summary: FLG (filaggrin) loss-of-function variants — R501X is one of the most common — cause severe atopic dermatitis (eczema), ichthyosis vulgaris, and predispose to asthma and food allergy via the 'atopic march'. Heterozygotes have ~3× eczema risk; homozygotes have severe presentations.
rs61816761.recommendation: If atopic: meticulous skin barrier care — daily ceramide-rich moisturizer (CeraVe, Cetaphil, Avène), short lukewarm showers with non-soap cleansers, avoid harsh detergents. Treat flares promptly with topical corticosteroids/tacrolimus per dermatologist. Children of carriers benefit from early aggressive moisturization (reduces eczema and food-allergy incidence).

rs10484554.name: rs10484554 (HLA-Cw6 proxy)
rs10484554.summary: rs10484554 tags HLA-Cw6 (HLA-C*06:02), the strongest single genetic risk factor for psoriasis (carriers have ~10× psoriasis risk; ~60% of psoriasis patients carry Cw6). Also associated with earlier-onset psoriasis and better response to certain biologics (e.g., ustekinumab).
rs10484554.recommendation: Carriage does not guarantee disease — many carriers are unaffected. If psoriasis develops or is present, modern treatments (topicals, phototherapy, methotrexate, IL-17 / IL-23 biologics) are highly effective. Trigger avoidance: streptococcal infections, smoking, heavy alcohol, stress, certain drugs (lithium, beta-blockers). Vitamin D sufficiency may help.

rs3827760.name: V370A (rs3827760)
rs3827760.summary: EDAR V370A is one of the strongest ancestry-informative markers — the G allele (V370A) is at >90% frequency in East Asian and Native American populations, near 0% in Europeans and Africans. It produces classic East Asian phenotypic traits: thicker, straighter hair shafts; more eccrine sweat glands; smaller breasts; characteristic shovel-shaped incisors.
rs3827760.recommendation: Phenotypic effects are normal variation, not health risks. Useful as an ancestry marker — strongly suggests East Asian or Native American ancestry.

rs16891982.name: L374F (rs16891982)
rs16891982.summary: SLC45A2 rs16891982 is another major European skin-lightening allele (alongside SLC24A5). The C allele (Phe374) is at >95% frequency in Europeans, much lower in other populations. Combined with SLC24A5, accounts for most of the depigmentation in West Eurasians.
rs16891982.recommendation: Same considerations as SLC24A5: lighter skin = more skin-cancer risk per UV dose AND more efficient vitamin D synthesis. Annual skin checks if fair-skinned with significant UV exposure history. Test 25-OH-D, supplement to keep ≥30–50 ng/mL.

rs10455872.name: rs10455872
rs10455872.summary: LPA rs10455872 G allele is one of the strongest common variants for elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], an LDL-like particle that is a strong independent risk factor for coronary artery disease, aortic stenosis, and stroke. Effect is largely unresponsive to statins and lifestyle.
rs10455872.recommendation: If positive: get a one-time Lp(a) blood test (mass or molar). If high (>50 mg/dL or >125 nmol/L), discuss aggressive control of other CV risk factors with your doctor: aim for ApoB ≤80 mg/dL, blood pressure ≤120/80, no smoking. Emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies (siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides) are in late-stage trials.

rs3798220.name: I4399M (rs3798220)
rs3798220.summary: LPA I4399M is another high-impact LPA variant — C allele is associated with markedly elevated Lp(a) levels and ~2-fold higher coronary heart disease risk. Less common than rs10455872 in Europeans but significant in many populations.
rs3798220.recommendation: Same as rs10455872 — measure Lp(a) once. If elevated, optimize all other CV risk factors aggressively. Statins do not lower Lp(a) (may slightly raise it); they still help via LDL-C reduction. Niacin and PCSK9 inhibitors lower Lp(a) modestly.

rs646776.name: rs646776 (1p13)
rs646776.summary: SORT1/CELSR2/PSRC1 locus rs646776 is one of the strongest non-LDLR/PCSK9 GWAS hits for LDL cholesterol and CHD. C allele raises LDL by ~5–10 mg/dL per copy and increases coronary risk ~15% per copy.
rs646776.recommendation: Standard LDL management: Mediterranean or DASH diet, soluble fiber (oats, beans, psyllium), regular exercise. If LDL persistently elevated, discuss statin/PCSK9 therapy with doctor based on full risk profile (ApoB, Lp(a), calcium score).

rs2383206.name: rs2383206
rs2383206.summary: 9p21 rs2383206 — another tag SNP for the strongest common CAD locus. Same biology and same risk-management implications as rs1333049.
rs2383206.recommendation: See rs1333049. Aggressive lifestyle CV management; consider CAC scan in midlife to refine risk.

rs1801252.name: S49G (rs1801252)
rs1801252.summary: ADRB1 S49G G allele is associated with altered beta-1 adrenergic receptor signalling, modest effects on resting heart rate and beta-blocker response (G allele may respond better to beta-blockade for hypertension/heart failure).
rs1801252.recommendation: Mostly relevant if on beta-blockers — discuss any side effects with prescriber. Generally not action-changing in absence of cardiac disease.

rs1801253.name: R389G (rs1801253)
rs1801253.summary: ADRB1 R389G C allele (Arg389) is associated with stronger beta-1 receptor signalling, better response to beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol) in heart failure, and modest differences in resting heart rate / hypertension risk.
rs1801253.recommendation: Mostly relevant for prescribers managing heart failure or hypertension. Genotype-guided beta-blocker selection is emerging but not yet routine.

rs5443.name: C825T (rs5443)
rs5443.summary: GNB3 C825T T allele is associated with enhanced G-protein signal transduction, increased risk of hypertension, obesity, depression, and altered antihypertensive response. Effect sizes are modest.
rs5443.recommendation: Standard hypertension prevention: DASH diet, sodium <2300 mg/day, ≥150 min aerobic exercise/week, alcohol moderation, maintain healthy weight.

rs699.name: M235T (rs699)
rs699.summary: AGT (angiotensinogen) M235T C allele (235T) is associated with higher plasma angiotensinogen, modestly increased BP and CV disease risk, and stronger response to sodium restriction.
rs699.recommendation: Carriers tend to be salt-sensitive — DASH diet and sodium restriction <2000 mg/day can have outsized benefit. Combine with potassium-rich foods (vegetables, beans, fruits).

rs2735940.name: rs2735940
rs2735940.summary: TERT promoter region rs2735940 G allele is associated with longer leukocyte telomere length and modest changes in risk for multiple cancers (lung adenocarcinoma, melanoma, glioma — slightly increased; some others slightly decreased).
rs2735940.recommendation: Effect is small. Standard cancer prevention: don't smoke, maintain healthy body composition, ≥150 min activity/week, limit alcohol, eat plant-rich diet, get UV-appropriate sun protection.

rs10993994.name: rs10993994 (PSP94)
rs10993994.summary: MSMB rs10993994 T allele is one of the more replicated common prostate-cancer risk variants (per-allele OR ~1.2). It is part of multiple prostate-cancer polygenic risk scores.
rs10993994.recommendation: Single SNP is not action-changing. If overall family/polygenic risk is elevated, discuss earlier or more frequent PSA screening (age 40–45) with a urologist. Avoid smoking; maintain healthy body composition.

rs1447295.name: rs1447295
rs1447295.summary: rs1447295 in the 8q24 prostate-cancer region — well-replicated common risk variant for prostate cancer (per-allele OR ~1.3). The 8q24 region contains multiple independent risk variants for prostate, colon, breast, and bladder cancers.
rs1447295.recommendation: Discuss with primary care: men with elevated polygenic risk benefit from informed PSA screening starting age 40–45. African-ancestry men have higher background prostate cancer risk and earlier screening is generally appropriate.

rs10505477.name: rs10505477
rs10505477.summary: CASC8 (cancer susceptibility 8) rs10505477 A allele is associated with modest increases in colorectal and prostate cancer risk. Effect size small.
rs10505477.recommendation: Standard CRC screening from age 45; consider earlier with family history. Avoid smoking, limit red/processed meat, eat fiber-rich plant foods, maintain healthy body composition, limit alcohol.

rs2735839.name: rs2735839
rs2735839.summary: KLK3 encodes prostate-specific antigen (PSA). rs2735839 G allele is associated with PSA levels and modest prostate cancer risk. Critical implication: this variant affects PSA levels independent of cancer, complicating PSA-based screening interpretation.
rs2735839.recommendation: Discuss with urologist about PSA-adjusted thresholds if applicable. PSA velocity, density, and isoforms (free PSA) may be more useful than a single PSA cutoff.

rs1801516.name: D1853N (rs1801516)
rs1801516.summary: ATM (ataxia-telangiectasia mutated) is involved in DNA-damage response. rs1801516 A allele (Asn1853) is a common variant with modest associations to breast cancer and radiation sensitivity. Rare ATM loss-of-function mutations confer substantial breast cancer risk.
rs1801516.recommendation: Common SNP itself is modestly action-changing. Strong family history of breast cancer warrants full BRCA + ATM + PALB2 + CHEK2 testing through a cancer genetics service.

rs861539.name: T241M (rs861539)
rs861539.summary: XRCC3 is involved in homologous recombination DNA repair. T241M T allele modestly increases risk of bladder cancer, skin cancer, and possibly breast cancer in some studies. Effect sizes are small.
rs861539.recommendation: Don't smoke, use UV protection, limit alcohol, eat antioxidant-rich diet. Standard cancer screening per age and family history.

rs1799782.name: R194W (rs1799782)
rs1799782.summary: XRCC1 R194W T allele has been associated with modest changes in DNA-damage repair efficiency and small increases in some cancer risks (lung, esophageal). Replication varies.
rs1799782.recommendation: Reduce DNA-damage exposures: smoking, UV without protection, excessive alcohol, processed/charred meat. Antioxidants from a varied plant-rich diet support DNA repair.

rs75932628.name: R47H (rs75932628)
rs75932628.summary: TREM2 R47H (T allele) is a rare-ish variant (~0.3% frequency in Europeans) that significantly increases Alzheimer's risk (OR ~2.5–4, similar to one copy of APOE-E4) by impairing microglial function in clearing amyloid. Also associated with frontotemporal dementia and Parkinson's risk.
rs75932628.recommendation: If positive, treat as a meaningful elevated AD risk signal. Same prevention as for APOE-E4: aerobic exercise, Mediterranean/MIND diet, quality sleep (7–9 h), cognitive engagement, BP/lipid control, hearing care. Consider discussing risk-reduction with a neurologist.

rs7274581.name: rs7274581
rs7274581.summary: CASS4 rs7274581 C allele is associated with modest Alzheimer's risk in GWAS — small effect, likely via amyloid and synaptic biology.
rs7274581.recommendation: Standard AD prevention: aerobic exercise, Mediterranean/MIND diet, sleep, cognitive and social engagement, BP/lipid control.

rs610932.name: rs610932
rs610932.summary: MS4A6A rs610932 — one of the modest-effect common variants identified in Alzheimer's GWAS. The MS4A gene cluster is involved in immune signalling.
rs610932.recommendation: Standard AD prevention. Effect is modest; lifestyle factors remain primary modifiable risks.

rs11218343.name: rs11218343
rs11218343.summary: SORL1 is involved in APP (amyloid precursor protein) trafficking. rs11218343 C allele (the protective allele) is associated with reduced Alzheimer's risk; some SORL1 rare variants cause familial early-onset AD.
rs11218343.recommendation: Standard AD prevention; the protective allele is a small favorable factor.

rs9275595.name: rs9275595
rs9275595.summary: HLA-DRB5/DRB1 region rs9275595 — a more recent Alzheimer's GWAS hit highlighting immune/neuroinflammation contribution.
rs9275595.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle: Mediterranean diet, omega-3s, regular exercise, sleep, stress management.

rs10498633.name: rs10498633
rs10498633.summary: SLC24A4 rs10498633 — modest common variant for Alzheimer's from GWAS. Calcium/potassium exchanger function may modulate neuronal calcium homeostasis.

rs11136000.name: rs11136000
rs11136000.summary: CLU (Clusterin) rs11136000 — the protective allele (C) reduces Alzheimer's risk modestly; T allele is the more common 'risk' allele in studies. CLU is involved in amyloid clearance.
rs11136000.recommendation: Same prevention as other AD loci.

rs1111875.name: rs1111875
rs1111875.summary: HHEX rs1111875 C allele is associated with increased type 2 diabetes risk (~15% per allele) via reduced beta-cell function.
rs1111875.recommendation: Standard T2D prevention: maintain healthy body composition, regular physical activity, fiber-rich diet, limit refined carbs and added sugars.

rs10010131.name: rs10010131
rs10010131.summary: WFS1 rs10010131 G allele is associated with modestly increased T2D risk. WFS1 mutations cause Wolfram syndrome (rare diabetes/neurological).

rs8050136.name: rs8050136
rs8050136.summary: FTO rs8050136 A allele — another tag SNP for the FTO obesity/diabetes locus. Effect is via increased body weight and food intake.
rs8050136.recommendation: Same as rs9939609: structured eating, higher-protein diet, daily physical activity overcome FTO effects.

rs1799884.name: rs1799884
rs1799884.summary: GCK (glucokinase) rs1799884 T allele is associated with slightly higher fasting glucose. GCK is the pancreatic and hepatic glucose sensor.
rs1799884.recommendation: Limit added sugars and refined starches; emphasize fiber and protein at meals. Walk after meals (10–15 min).

rs1799983.name: G894T (rs1799983)
rs1799983.summary: NOS3 (endothelial nitric oxide synthase) G894T T allele is associated with reduced NO production, modestly elevated blood pressure, reduced exercise capacity, and somewhat impaired endothelial function.
rs1799983.recommendation: Boost NO naturally: nitrate-rich vegetables (beets, leafy greens — arugula, spinach), regular aerobic exercise (improves eNOS expression), adequate vitamin D, L-citrulline 3–6 g/day for those interested in supplementation.

rs602662.name: rs602662
rs602662.summary: FUT2 rs602662 G allele tags a haplotype affecting blood-group secretor status, gut microbiome composition (Bifidobacteria abundance), and serum vitamin B12 levels.
rs602662.recommendation: Non-secretors may benefit from probiotic Bifidobacteria support (live-culture foods: kefir, yogurt, kimchi). Test functional B12 markers (MMA, holo-TC) rather than just serum B12 if symptomatic.

rs2282679.name: rs2282679 (vitamin D binding protein)
rs2282679.summary: GC encodes vitamin D binding protein (DBP); rs2282679 C allele is associated with lower total 25-OH-vitamin D levels and reduced response to oral vitamin D supplementation. Effects on bioavailable vitamin D are more complex.
rs2282679.recommendation: Test 25-OH-D rather than estimating from intake. Maintain levels 30–50 ng/mL. Higher supplementation doses (2000–4000 IU/day) may be needed for C/C homozygotes. Sun exposure remains an effective source.

rs10741657.name: rs10741657
rs10741657.summary: CYP2R1 rs10741657 G allele is associated with lower 25-hydroxylase activity and lower 25-OH-D levels. CYP2R1 converts vitamin D3 to 25-OH-D in the liver.
rs10741657.recommendation: Same as rs2282679 — test 25-OH-D, dose based on result. Combine D3 with K2 (MK-7) and adequate magnesium for downstream effects.

rs4994.name: W64R (rs4994)
rs4994.summary: ADRB3 W64R G allele is associated with reduced beta-3 adrenergic signalling, somewhat lower thermogenesis in brown/beige fat, and modest associations with metabolic syndrome traits.
rs4994.recommendation: Adequate cold exposure (brief cold showers, cool ambient temperatures), regular aerobic exercise, and protein at meals all support thermogenesis.

rs1572312.name: rs1572312
rs1572312.summary: NFE2L2 (NRF2) rs1572312 is a regulatory variant for the master antioxidant transcription factor. Variants in this region modestly affect exercise-induced oxidative stress and adaptation.
rs1572312.recommendation: Periodize antioxidant supplementation — high-dose vitamin C/E around training can blunt adaptations. Whole-food polyphenols (berries, green tea, dark chocolate) are fine and supportive.

rs1042713.name: R16G (rs1042713)
rs1042713.summary: ADRB2 R16G (G = Gly16) is associated with altered beta-2 receptor responses — affects bronchodilator response (asthma), VO2max trainability, and lipolysis with exercise.
rs1042713.recommendation: Asthmatics with G/G may have different inhaler response — discuss with pulmonologist. For training, normal response patterns; aerobic adaptation is robust across genotypes.

rs17602729.name: Q12X (rs17602729)
rs17602729.summary: AMPD1 Q12X (T allele = stop) abolishes muscle adenosine monophosphate deaminase activity in homozygotes — associated with exercise-induced muscle cramps, fatigue, and reduced anaerobic performance. Heterozygotes are mostly asymptomatic.
rs17602729.recommendation: Heterozygotes: usually no issue. Homozygotes: if experiencing exercise intolerance / cramping, ensure hydration, electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium), and gradual progression. Discuss with a sports-medicine physician if symptomatic.

rs12248560.name: *17 (rs12248560)
rs12248560.summary: CYP2C19 *17 (T allele) is an increased-function allele — ultra-rapid metabolizers clear CYP2C19 substrates faster. For clopidogrel this is favorable (better activation); for PPIs and some SSRIs this can mean lower drug exposure and reduced efficacy.
rs12248560.recommendation: Inform prescribers if starting PPI or SSRI — dose may need adjustment if response is inadequate. Generally favorable for clopidogrel response.

rs776746.name: *3 (rs776746)
rs776746.summary: CYP3A5 *3 (C allele) is a splice variant that essentially eliminates CYP3A5 protein in C/C individuals — the most common genotype in Europeans (~85%). Heavily impacts tacrolimus dosing in transplant patients: expressors (T/T, T/C) need ~2× the dose of non-expressors (C/C).
rs776746.recommendation: Critical for transplant recipients on tacrolimus — modern protocols include CYP3A5 genotyping. For non-transplant use, less actionable but worth noting.

rs2032582.name: G2677T/A (rs2032582)
rs2032582.summary: ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) rs2032582 affects efflux of many drugs across blood-brain barrier and intestinal epithelium. Effect sizes are small and drug-specific.
rs2032582.recommendation: Single SNP effects are modest. ABCB1 status may be relevant for some chemotherapy drugs, immunosuppressants, and antiepileptics — prescribers integrate this when relevant.

rs887829.name: *28 promoter (rs887829 proxy)
rs887829.summary: UGT1A1 *28 (TA7 promoter repeat) reduces bilirubin glucuronidation, causing Gilbert syndrome (benign mild jaundice) and significantly affecting irinotecan toxicity (severe neutropenia, diarrhea in *28/*28 homozygotes). rs887829 is a common tag SNP for *28 status.
rs887829.recommendation: Generally harmless (Gilbert is benign). If considering irinotecan for cancer, UGT1A1 genotyping should be performed — dose reduction recommended in homozygotes.

rs2306283.name: N130D (rs2306283)
rs2306283.summary: SLCO1B1 is involved in hepatic uptake of many drugs including statins. rs2306283 is part of haplotype definitions; the *15 haplotype (with rs4149056) increases simvastatin-induced myopathy risk substantially.
rs2306283.recommendation: Particularly relevant when starting high-dose statins. If muscle symptoms develop, switch to rosuvastatin or pravastatin (less SLCO1B1-dependent), or lower the dose.

rs1979277.name: rs1979277
rs1979277.summary: SHMT1 (serine hydroxymethyltransferase 1) rs1979277 A allele is associated with modestly altered folate metabolism — shifts folate flux between DNA synthesis and methylation pathways.
rs1979277.recommendation: Adequate folate intake (methylfolate or food sources: leafy greens, legumes). Particularly relevant if combined with MTHFR variants.

rs7946.name: V175M (rs7946)
rs7946.summary: PEMT (phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase) converts PE to PC using SAMe — accounts for ~30% of choline-derived phosphatidylcholine. rs7946 T allele reduces enzyme activity; in combination with low choline intake increases NAFLD and choline-deficiency-related risks. Effect is amplified by estrogen-deficient states (post-menopause).
rs7946.recommendation: Ensure adequate dietary choline (eggs — 2/day provides ~300 mg; meat, fish, dairy, cruciferous vegetables). RDI: 425 mg/day women, 550 mg/day men. Particularly important during pregnancy and in low-estrogen states.

rs20417.name: rs20417
rs20417.summary: PTGS2 (COX-2) rs20417 C allele is associated with altered COX-2 expression — may modulate response to NSAIDs and underlying inflammatory tone. Some studies link C allele to increased cardiovascular risk in inflammation-prone individuals.
rs20417.recommendation: Manage modifiable inflammation drivers: Mediterranean diet, omega-3s (1–2 g EPA+DHA/day), regular exercise, adequate sleep, stress management.

rs2228145.name: D358A (rs2228145)
rs2228145.summary: IL6R rs2228145 C allele is associated with altered IL-6 receptor signalling, with implications similar to tocilizumab (IL-6R blocker) — lower CRP, modestly reduced cardiovascular event rate, and possible reduced autoimmune flares.
rs2228145.recommendation: Generally favorable variant. Continue anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Tocilizumab effects in C/C carriers may be somewhat blunted (they have intrinsically lower IL-6R signalling).

rs2104286.name: rs2104286
rs2104286.summary: IL2RA rs2104286 — implicated in T-cell regulation and autoimmune disease (multiple sclerosis, type 1 diabetes) susceptibility.
rs2104286.recommendation: Vitamin D sufficiency, omega-3s, smoking avoidance, normal body composition support immune regulation.

rs73598374.name: rs73598374
rs73598374.summary: ADA (adenosine deaminase) rs73598374 A allele is associated with deeper slow-wave sleep (more time in N3) and stronger response to caffeine — adenosine clears more slowly.
rs73598374.recommendation: Limit caffeine to mornings if A/A. Take advantage of deeper sleep — prioritize consistent bedtime and dark environment.

rs12649507.name: rs12649507
rs12649507.summary: ARNTL (BMAL1) rs12649507 is part of the core circadian clock and is associated with sleep duration and metabolic-health interactions with sleep.
rs12649507.recommendation: Regular sleep-wake schedule, morning light exposure, evening dimming — strongest levers for circadian alignment.

rs2200733.name: rs2200733
rs2200733.summary: Note: this is the strongest atrial-fibrillation common GWAS hit; included here as a frequently-typed variant. T allele increases atrial fibrillation risk ~1.7× per copy.
rs2200733.recommendation: Maintain BP <130/80, normal body weight, treat sleep apnea if present, limit alcohol (>7 drinks/week markedly raises AFib risk), exercise but avoid extreme endurance loads which paradoxically raise AFib risk in some.

rs3135388.name: rs3135388 (HLA-DR15 proxy)
rs3135388.summary: rs3135388 A allele tags HLA-DRB1*15:01, the main multiple sclerosis risk haplotype (per-allele OR ~3, accounting for ~10% of MS heritability). Also associated with response to anti-thymocyte globulin and certain drug hypersensitivities.
rs3135388.recommendation: Carriage does not predict MS — vast majority of carriers never develop MS. If MS symptoms (vision changes, numbness, balance problems, fatigue), see a neurologist promptly. Vitamin D sufficiency (≥40 ng/mL) is associated with reduced MS risk.

rs2542151.name: rs2542151
rs2542151.summary: PTPN2 rs2542151 G allele is associated with type 1 diabetes, celiac disease, Crohn's disease, and rheumatoid arthritis — a broad autoimmune-susceptibility locus.
rs2542151.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Watch for autoimmune signs (unexplained weight loss, joint pain, persistent fatigue, skin changes); see a rheumatologist or appropriate specialist if present.

rs2241880.name: T300A (rs2241880)
rs2241880.summary: ATG16L1 T300A G allele is associated with Crohn's disease risk via altered autophagy. Effect compounds with NOD2 variants and smoking.
rs2241880.recommendation: Don't smoke (strongest modifiable Crohn's risk). Mediterranean-style diet. If GI symptoms (chronic diarrhea, blood, weight loss), see gastroenterology.

rs1990760.name: A946T (rs1990760)
rs1990760.summary: IFIH1 A946T T allele alters innate antiviral signalling and is associated with type 1 diabetes, lupus, and psoriasis susceptibility.
rs1990760.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Vitamin D sufficiency. Routine vaccinations as usual.

rs1800872.name: -592 A/C (rs1800872)
rs1800872.summary: IL10 -592 A allele is associated with lower IL-10 production and inflammatory-disease susceptibility — part of the IL10 haplotype with rs1800896.
rs1800872.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle as in IL-10 rs1800896.

rs78378222.name: rs78378222 (3'-UTR)
rs78378222.summary: TP53 3'-UTR rs78378222 G allele is associated with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, and glioma. Effect sizes are modest.
rs78378222.recommendation: UV protection; annual skin exams if fair-skinned. Avoid sunbeds.

rs1056827.name: rs1056827
rs1056827.summary: CYP1B1 rs1056827 T allele is associated with altered metabolism of estrogens, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and some drugs. Effect on 4-hydroxylation of estradiol has implications for estrogen-driven cancers.
rs1056827.recommendation: See rs1056836 (CYP1B1 L432V). Phase II support via sulforaphane/cruciferous vegetables. Limit xenobiotic exposures (smoking, charred meat, alcohol).

rs6413432.name: rs6413432
rs6413432.summary: CYP2E1 metabolizes ethanol, acetone, and many low-molecular-weight xenobiotics — generates reactive intermediates that can be harmful. rs6413432 affects expression / inducibility.
rs6413432.recommendation: Limit alcohol — CYP2E1 is induced by chronic alcohol and amplifies acetaminophen hepatotoxicity. Don't combine high-dose acetaminophen with regular drinking. Support glutathione (NAC, sulfur amino acids).

rs8176719.name: rs8176719 (non-O blood group)
rs8176719.summary: ABO blood-group locus rs8176719 — non-O blood groups (A, B, AB) have higher von Willebrand factor and Factor VIII, with associated higher VTE and arterial thrombosis risk (~1.5–2×) compared to type O.
rs8176719.recommendation: Stay hydrated and active during long flights/immobility, particularly with other thrombophilia variants. Discuss with doctor before estrogen-containing contraceptives or hormone therapy if multiple thrombosis risk factors.

rs6046.name: R353Q (rs6046)
rs6046.summary: F7 R353Q A allele is associated with lower Factor VII levels and slightly reduced cardiovascular event risk.
rs6046.recommendation: Favorable for arterial thrombosis risk; no specific action needed.

rs6275.name: rs6275 (synonymous)
rs6275.summary: DRD2 rs6275 — synonymous variant in DRD2; part of haplotypes affecting D2 receptor expression and tagged with broader DRD2 dopaminergic phenotype.
rs6275.recommendation: Standard mental health support: exercise (best evidence for BDNF/dopamine), sleep, social connection, meaningful work, limit alcohol.

rs1611115.name: -1021 C/T (rs1611115)
rs1611115.summary: DBH (dopamine beta-hydroxylase) -1021 T allele is associated with lower DBH activity, lower noradrenaline levels (more dopamine relative to NE), and modest associations with ADHD, smoking response, and stimulant side effects.
rs1611115.recommendation: Pair stimulant medications (if prescribed) with careful monitoring of cardiovascular/anxiety side effects. Aerobic exercise and L-tyrosine 500–2000 mg before cognitively demanding tasks may support catecholamine availability.

rs11591147.name: R46L (rs11591147)
rs11591147.summary: PCSK9 R46L (T allele = Leu46) is a loss-of-function variant that lowers LDL cholesterol by ~15 mg/dL per copy and reduces coronary heart disease risk ~40% per copy. Carriers have lifelong lower LDL exposure — proof-of-concept for PCSK9 inhibitors.
rs11591147.recommendation: Favorable variant; standard CV prevention applies. If unrelated to this variant you have high LDL, PCSK9 inhibitors (alirocumab, evolocumab) are highly effective. Statins remain first-line.

rs6511720.name: rs6511720
rs6511720.summary: LDLR rs6511720 T allele is associated with lower LDL cholesterol (~5–7 mg/dL per copy) and reduced coronary heart disease risk via greater LDL receptor expression.

rs2943641.name: rs2943641
rs2943641.summary: IRS1 (insulin receptor substrate 1) rs2943641 C allele is associated with insulin resistance and increased T2D risk. Effect is reduced by physical activity.
rs2943641.recommendation: Resistance training (insulin-sensitizing) plus aerobic activity. Mediterranean diet rich in olive oil and fish.

rs17228212.name: rs17228212
rs17228212.summary: SMAD3 rs17228212 — common variant in TGF-β signalling locus, modestly associated with CAD risk.

rs599839.name: rs599839
rs599839.summary: rs599839 — robust GWAS hit for LDL cholesterol and coronary heart disease, near the SORT1 region.

rs17465637.name: rs17465637
rs17465637.summary: MIA3 rs17465637 — replicated GWAS variant for CAD with modest effect.

rs10757278.name: rs10757278
rs10757278.summary: 9p21 rs10757278 G allele increases CAD risk ~25–30% per copy. The 9p21 region is the strongest non-lipid CAD locus.
rs10757278.recommendation: Aggressive CV prevention: BP <120/80, ApoB <80, no smoking, ≥150 min aerobic + ≥2 resistance/week, Mediterranean diet, 7–9 h sleep. Consider CAC scan ≥40.

rs2549513.name: W719R proxy
rs2549513.summary: KIF6 W719R has been controversially associated with CHD and statin response in some studies. Recent large analyses suggest minimal effect.
rs2549513.recommendation: Not strongly action-changing. Statin decisions on standard risk criteria.

rs401681.name: rs401681
rs401681.summary: rs401681 in the TERT-CLPTM1L region — pleiotropic cancer locus with modest associations to multiple cancers (lung, bladder, melanoma, pancreatic).
rs401681.recommendation: Don't smoke. UV protection. Standard cancer screening per age and family history.

rs4779584.name: rs4779584
rs4779584.summary: rs4779584 — common variant near GREM1 associated with modest colorectal cancer risk.
rs4779584.recommendation: Standard CRC screening from age 45; consider earlier with family history.

rs2981579.name: rs2981579
rs2981579.summary: FGFR2 rs2981579 A allele is another tag SNP for the FGFR2 breast cancer haplotype, with effect overlapping rs2981582.
rs2981579.recommendation: Breast cancer polygenic risk score evaluation if family history. Standard screening per guidelines.

rs1801320.name: G135C (rs1801320)
rs1801320.summary: RAD51 G135C C allele has been variably associated with breast and ovarian cancer risk in BRCA carriers — a risk modifier rather than primary driver.
rs1801320.recommendation: Particularly relevant if BRCA1/2 carrier — discuss with genetic counselor.

rs1052133.name: S326C (rs1052133)
rs1052133.summary: OGG1 (8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase) S326C G allele has reduced repair activity for oxidative DNA damage; associated with several cancers (lung, esophageal, gastric).
rs1052133.recommendation: Antioxidant-rich plant diet; don't smoke; limit alcohol; minimize charred meat.

rs713598.name: rs713598 (PTC taster)
rs713598.summary: TAS2R38 rs713598 — together with rs1726866 and rs10246939 defines PAV/AVI haplotype for bitterness perception (PTC/PROP). PAV haplotype = strong taster; AVI = non-taster. Affects vegetable preferences, alcohol intake, smoking preferences.
rs713598.recommendation: Strong tasters often dislike cruciferous vegetables — try light steaming + olive oil/lemon, roasting (caramelizes bitterness), or smoothies blended with sweet fruit.

rs1726866.name: rs1726866
rs1726866.summary: TAS2R38 rs1726866 — second of three SNPs defining the PAV/AVI bitter-taster haplotype.

rs10246939.name: rs10246939
rs10246939.summary: TAS2R38 rs10246939 — third of three SNPs defining the PTC/PROP bitter-taster haplotype.

rs182549.name: rs182549 (lactase persistence)
rs182549.summary: rs182549 (and rs4988235) define European-style lactase persistence — T allele carriers continue producing lactase into adulthood. C/C individuals have lactase non-persistence and may develop bloating, diarrhea after dairy.
rs182549.recommendation: If lactase non-persistent: limit milk; cultured dairy (yogurt, kefir) and aged cheeses are usually tolerated. Lactose-free milk or lactase enzyme supplements as needed.

rs5400.name: T110I (rs5400)
rs5400.summary: GLUT2 rs5400 T allele is associated with higher dietary sugar intake — variant carriers may have somewhat altered sweetness perception or central reward response to sugar.
rs5400.recommendation: Reduce added sugars (<25 g/day women, <36 g/day men). Use natural sweetness from fruit; mindful eating practices.

rs9826737.name: rs9826737
rs9826737.summary: rs9826737 has been studied in lipid GWAS — modest association with HDL.

rs1057868.name: A503V (rs1057868)
rs1057868.summary: POR (P450 oxidoreductase) provides electrons to all microsomal CYP enzymes. A503V is a common variant with modest effects on substrate-specific CYP activity.
rs1057868.recommendation: Effect is drug-specific and modest. Inform prescriber if multiple CYP-related side effects.

rs2070676.name: rs2070676
rs2070676.summary: CYP2E1 rs2070676 affects expression. CYP2E1 metabolizes ethanol, acetaminophen, and many low-MW xenobiotics.
rs2070676.recommendation: Don't combine high-dose acetaminophen with regular alcohol use.

rs2231142.name: Q141K (rs2231142)
rs2231142.summary: ABCG2 Q141K T allele reduces transport activity, affecting uric acid excretion (gout risk) and drug efflux (rosuvastatin, methotrexate, allopurinol — higher plasma levels).
rs2231142.recommendation: If diagnosed with gout, this variant predicts allopurinol/febuxostat response. With rosuvastatin, lower starting doses may suffice in T allele carriers.

rs9332377.summary: CYP2C9 *5 variant (less common than *2/*3) — additional reduced-function allele affecting warfarin, phenytoin, NSAIDs.
rs9332377.recommendation: Same as CYP2C9 *2/*3 — flag if starting warfarin, phenytoin, etc.

rs6428370.name: D85Y (rs6428370 proxy)
rs6428370.summary: UGT2B15 glucuronidates lorazepam, oxazepam, and some androgens. Variants affect drug clearance; effect sizes are modest.
rs6428370.recommendation: Most relevant when prescribers consider benzodiazepine selection in elderly patients (lorazepam often preferred for shorter half-life and renal safety).

rs864745.name: rs864745
rs864745.summary: JAZF1 rs864745 T allele is associated with modestly increased T2D risk via reduced insulin secretion.

rs1801214.name: R611H (rs1801214)
rs1801214.summary: WFS1 rs1801214 — another WFS1 locus variant associated with modestly increased T2D risk.

rs6552828.name: rs6552828
rs6552828.summary: ACVR1B variants are associated with muscle mass and strength — effect sizes are modest.
rs6552828.recommendation: Resistance training 2–3× weekly with adequate protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg/day) drives muscle growth regardless of genotype.

rs6280.name: S9G (rs6280)
rs6280.summary: DRD3 S9G — dopamine D3 receptor variant associated with treatment response to antipsychotics, modest impulsivity associations.
rs6280.recommendation: Mental-health treatment decisions are clinical; this is background context only.

rs1799978.name: -241 (rs1799978)
rs1799978.summary: DRD2 promoter rs1799978 — additional DRD2 regulatory variant affecting dopaminergic phenotype.

rs7517847.name: rs7517847
rs7517847.summary: IL23R rs7517847 T allele is protective against inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and ankylosing spondylitis — illustrates IL-23/IL-17 axis importance.
rs7517847.recommendation: Background context. If IBD/AS symptoms develop, modern biologics targeting IL-23 (ustekinumab, risankizumab) are highly effective.

rs11209026.name: R381Q (rs11209026)
rs11209026.summary: IL23R R381Q (A = Gln381) is a strong protective variant against Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, psoriasis, and ankylosing spondylitis (per-allele OR ~0.4 for IBD).
rs11209026.recommendation: Favorable variant. If IBD/AS still develops, IL-23 pathway biologics remain effective options.

rs1200638.name: rs1200638
rs1200638.summary: CCR6 rs1200638 — associated with multiple autoimmune diseases via Th17 trafficking.
rs1200638.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle; standard autoimmune screening per family history.

rs3957357.name: rs3957357
rs3957357.summary: GSTA1 rs3957357 — promoter variant affecting glutathione transferase A1 expression. Higher expression confers better detoxification of some pharmaceuticals.
rs3957357.recommendation: Support glutathione: NAC 600 mg twice daily if oxidative stress is high; sulfur amino acids (eggs, garlic, cruciferous vegetables).

rs3781638.name: rs3781638
rs3781638.summary: ABCC9 rs3781638 — associated with sleep duration; effect size small.
rs3781638.recommendation: Consistent sleep timing; 7–9 h nightly; morning light exposure; limit evening screens.

rs3825942.name: G153D (rs3825942)
rs3825942.summary: LOXL1 rs3825942 G allele is strongly associated with pseudoexfoliation glaucoma. Risk is geographically variable — highest in Northern Europeans, low in African ancestry. Carriers can still avoid glaucoma; non-carriers occasionally develop it.
rs3825942.recommendation: Regular eye exams from age 40 — every 2–4 years; annually after 60. Pseudoexfoliation is one of the strongest risk factors for open-angle glaucoma.

rs763035.name: rs763035
rs763035.summary: rs763035 is a tag for HLA-B*57:01, the allele associated with severe hypersensitivity to abacavir (HIV drug). Carriers must NOT receive abacavir.
rs763035.recommendation: If diagnosed with HIV, ensure HLA-B*57:01 status is checked before abacavir prescription. This is standard of care globally.

rs9272346.name: rs9272346
rs9272346.summary: HLA-DQA1 rs9272346 G allele tags type 1 diabetes risk haplotypes (DR3-DQ2 and DR4-DQ8 regions).
rs9272346.recommendation: Children with family history of T1D and high-risk HLA: discuss islet-autoantibody screening (TrialNet). Vitamin D sufficiency may reduce T1D risk.

rs1265181.name: rs1265181
rs1265181.summary: CCHCR1 — psoriasis-associated locus in MHC class I region.
rs1265181.recommendation: Standard anti-inflammatory lifestyle; biologics if psoriasis develops.

rs12203592.name: rs12203592
rs12203592.summary: IRF4 rs12203592 T allele is associated with lighter pigmentation, freckles, increased nevus count, and somewhat elevated melanoma risk — particularly in fair-skinned individuals.
rs12203592.recommendation: UV protection: daily broad-spectrum SPF 30+, wide-brim hat, UV-protective clothing. Annual skin checks if fair-skinned and many moles.

rs1799990.name: M129V (rs1799990)
rs1799990.summary: PRNP M129V — homozygosity (either MM or VV) is associated with greatly increased susceptibility to prion diseases (CJD, variant CJD). Heterozygotes are partly protected.
rs1799990.recommendation: Avoid potential prion exposures (high-risk medical/lab settings have protocols). No specific dietary action for general population.

rs3818361.name: rs3818361
rs3818361.summary: CR1 rs3818361 — additional Alzheimer's-associated CR1 locus variant.

rs1525892.name: rs1525892
rs1525892.summary: TF (transferrin) rs1525892 is associated with serum iron and transferrin levels.
rs1525892.recommendation: If symptomatic iron deficiency or overload, full iron-panel + ferritin testing.

rs1051266.name: G80A (rs1051266)
rs1051266.summary: SLC19A1 (reduced folate carrier) G80A A allele reduces folate transport into cells. Relevant for methotrexate response (lower intracellular methotrexate) and folate metabolism.
rs1051266.recommendation: Methylfolate (5-MTHF) preferred over folic acid. Particularly important if MTHFR variants present.

rs10380.name: rs10380
rs10380.summary: MTRR rs10380 — additional MTRR locus variant, affecting B12-dependent methylation.

rs1801019.name: T-34C (rs1801019)
rs1801019.summary: CYP17A1 is required for androgen and estrogen biosynthesis. T-34C C allele is associated with higher estrogen levels in women and modest effects on androgens.
rs1801019.recommendation: Standard hormone-supportive lifestyle: sleep, training, body composition, healthy fats, micronutrient sufficiency (zinc, vitamin D, magnesium).

rs4316682.name: rs4316682
rs4316682.summary: LIN28B rs4316682 is associated with timing of puberty and adult height. Indirect effects on hormonal trajectory.
rs4316682.recommendation: No specific action for adults; relevant in pediatric endocrinology contexts.

rs2811712.name: rs2811712
rs2811712.summary: ANRIL long non-coding RNA at 9p21 — additional variant in this pleiotropic locus implicated in CAD, T2D, cancer, longevity.
rs2811712.recommendation: Standard healthy-aging lifestyle: Mediterranean diet, exercise, sleep, stress management, social connection.

rs6151429.name: rs6151429
rs6151429.summary: PRM1 (protamine 1) is essential for sperm chromatin compaction. Common variants modestly affect sperm parameters; rare LOF variants cause infertility.
rs6151429.recommendation: Standard sperm-quality optimization: avoid heat (hot tubs, laptop on lap), zinc 25 mg/day, CoQ10 200 mg/day, L-carnitine 1–2 g/day, healthy weight, no smoking, limit alcohol.

rs7224550.name: rs7224550
rs7224550.summary: PRM2 (protamine 2) — second major sperm-chromatin protein. Variants modestly affect male fertility parameters.
rs7224550.recommendation: Same as PRM1: targeted sperm-quality optimization if trying to conceive.

rs28371725.name: *41 (rs28371725)
rs28371725.summary: CYP2D6 *41 (T allele) is a reduced-function allele — important for predicting atomoxetine clearance and CYP2D6 phenotype overall.
rs28371725.recommendation: Combined with other CYP2D6 variants determines phenotype (poor / intermediate / normal / ultra-rapid metabolizer). Inform psychiatrist of CYP2D6 variants when starting atomoxetine or SSRIs primarily metabolized by 2D6.

rs2814778.name: Duffy null (rs2814778)
rs2814778.summary: rs2814778 C allele abolishes Duffy antigen expression on red blood cells — at near-fixation (~95%+) in West/Central African populations, ~0% elsewhere. Duffy null confers resistance to P. vivax malaria but is associated with lower neutrophil counts (benign ethnic neutropenia).
rs2814778.recommendation: Duffy-null individuals: 'low' neutrophil counts on standard labs (often 1000–2000) may be normal — not indicative of disease. Inform doctors before chemotherapy decisions based on neutropenia thresholds.

rs17822931.name: G180R (rs17822931)
rs17822931.summary: ABCC11 rs17822931 T allele (T/T) is associated with dry earwax type and minimal axillary odor — at high frequency in East Asian and Native American populations, low in Europeans and Africans (who almost all have C, wet earwax, stronger body odor).
rs17822931.recommendation: Phenotypic effect, not health risk. T/T individuals produce very little apocrine sweat and may not need deodorant. Strong ancestry marker.

rs1129038.name: rs1129038
rs1129038.summary: HERC2 rs1129038 — second tag SNP for the major European blue-eye haplotype (alongside rs12913832). Strong European-ancestry marker.
rs1129038.recommendation: Eye color is not a health risk; lighter irises have slightly less natural UV protection — use UV-blocking sunglasses.

rs2402130.name: rs2402130
rs2402130.summary: rs2402130 — additional EDAR-locus variant in the East Asian / Native American hair-thickness sweep, complements rs3827760.

rs6905288.name: rs6905288
rs6905288.summary: rs6905288 — replicated GWAS variant near VAV3 with modest blood-pressure effect.
rs6905288.recommendation: Standard BP management; DASH diet, exercise, sleep, sodium <2300 mg/d.

rs11969344.name: rs11969344
rs11969344.summary: CDH13 (T-cadherin) variant — modest association with cardiovascular outcomes and adiponectin levels.

rs12740374.name: rs12740374
rs12740374.summary: rs12740374 T allele is the causal variant at the SORT1 locus — disrupts a C/EBP binding site, raising hepatic SORT1 expression and elevating LDL ~5–10 mg/dL per copy.
rs12740374.recommendation: Standard lipid management; ApoB on lipid panels.

rs602633.name: rs602633
rs602633.summary: rs602633 — additional tag SNP for the 1p13 SORT1/CELSR2 LDL locus.

rs7173743.name: rs7173743
rs7173743.summary: rs7173743 — GWAS-replicated CAD variant; modest effect.

rs2736098.name: A1062T proxy
rs2736098.summary: TERT rs2736098 affects telomerase activity; A allele is associated with multiple cancer susceptibilities (lung, bladder, melanoma).
rs2736098.recommendation: Don't smoke. UV protection. Standard cancer screening.

rs1011970.name: rs1011970
rs1011970.summary: CDKN2A/B (9p21) rs1011970 — modest melanoma and basal cell carcinoma association.
rs1011970.recommendation: UV protection; annual skin checks if fair-skinned.

rs2274223.name: rs2274223
rs2274223.summary: PLCE1 rs2274223 G allele has been associated with esophageal cancer (especially in East Asian populations) and gastric cardia cancer.
rs2274223.recommendation: Don't smoke. Limit alcohol (synergistic with ALDH2). Treat H. pylori.

rs2853669.name: rs2853669
rs2853669.summary: TERT promoter rs2853669 — interacts with TERT promoter mutations seen in some cancers (glioma, melanoma, hepatocellular).

rs1799966.name: S1613G proxy (rs1799966)
rs1799966.summary: BRCA1 rs1799966 is a common synonymous variant in BRCA1; not pathogenic itself but used to tag haplotypes. NOT a substitute for full BRCA1/2 sequencing.
rs1799966.recommendation: For breast/ovarian cancer family history, only full BRCA1/2/ATM/PALB2/CHEK2 panel testing through a genetic counselor is informative.

rs3218536.name: R188H (rs3218536)
rs3218536.summary: XRCC2 R188H — DNA repair variant with modest associations to breast and pancreatic cancer.
rs3218536.recommendation: Standard cancer screening per family history; don't smoke.

rs6232.name: rs6232
rs6232.summary: PCSK1 rs6232 has been associated with obesity and altered satiety hormone processing.
rs6232.recommendation: Higher-protein diet (1.6 g/kg) and structured meal timing improve satiety.

rs2287019.name: rs2287019
rs2287019.summary: GIPR rs2287019 — incretin receptor variant associated with postprandial glucose and BMI.
rs2287019.recommendation: Walk 10–15 min after meals; limit refined carbohydrates.

rs41423247.name: BclI (rs41423247)
rs41423247.summary: NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) BclI G allele is associated with increased cortisol sensitivity — may amplify stress effects, modest association with depression and metabolic syndrome.
rs41423247.recommendation: Daily stress management: meditation, exercise, sleep, social connection. Limit chronic stressors where possible; psychotherapy if persistent stress affects function.

rs6295.name: C-1019G (rs6295)
rs6295.summary: HTR1A rs6295 G allele is associated with reduced 5-HT1A autoreceptor regulation, depression susceptibility, and antidepressant response variation.
rs6295.recommendation: Treatment decisions are clinical. Augment with exercise, light, sleep, omega-3s, structured psychotherapy.

rs2230912.name: rs2230912
rs2230912.summary: PER3 (circadian clock) variants — associated with morning vs. evening chronotype, sleep, and mood-circadian interactions.
rs2230912.recommendation: Maintain consistent sleep-wake schedule; morning light; evening dimming.

rs2070874.name: rs2070874
rs2070874.summary: IL4 rs2070874 — associated with allergic disease, asthma, and IgE levels.
rs2070874.recommendation: Allergen avoidance where feasible. Discuss biologics (dupilumab) with allergist for severe atopic disease.

rs20541.name: R130Q (rs20541)
rs20541.summary: IL13 R130Q T allele is associated with asthma, atopic dermatitis, and allergic rhinitis. IL-13 drives Th2 inflammation.
rs20541.recommendation: Allergen reduction; for severe atopic disease, IL-4/IL-13 pathway biologics (dupilumab) are highly effective.

rs2069837.name: rs2069837
rs2069837.summary: IL6 rs2069837 — additional IL6-locus regulatory variant.

rs231775.name: +49 (rs231775)
rs231775.summary: CTLA4 rs231775 G allele is associated with multiple autoimmune diseases (Graves' disease, autoimmune thyroiditis, T1D, lupus). CTLA-4 is a key T-cell brake.
rs231775.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle; thyroid function (TSH) screening every few years; watch for autoimmune symptoms.

rs7997012.name: rs7997012
rs7997012.summary: HTR2A rs7997012 — associated with citalopram/escitalopram response in some studies.
rs7997012.recommendation: Treatment selection is clinical; structured outcome measurement (PHQ-9) when starting any antidepressant.

rs1801028.name: S311C (rs1801028)
rs1801028.summary: DRD2 S311C — antipsychotic response variant; small effect.

rs116855232.name: R139C (rs116855232)
rs116855232.summary: NUDT15 R139C is a critical thiopurine sensitivity variant in East Asian populations (and present elsewhere). Carriers experience severe leukopenia on standard azathioprine/6-MP doses.
rs116855232.recommendation: Test NUDT15 (alongside TPMT) before thiopurines, particularly in East Asian patients.

rs10885122.name: rs10885122
rs10885122.summary: ADRA2A rs10885122 — associated with fasting glucose via altered beta-cell adrenergic signalling.

rs2191349.name: rs2191349
rs2191349.summary: rs2191349 — replicated fasting glucose / T2D variant.

rs17561.name: +4845 G/T (rs17561)
rs17561.summary: IL1A rs17561 — associated with inflammatory disease susceptibility; modest effect.

rs1800469.name: rs1800469
rs1800469.summary: TGFB1 rs1800469 — affects TGF-β1 expression; associated with fibrosis-related conditions.
rs1800469.recommendation: Anti-inflammatory lifestyle; treat sleep apnea if present (chronic hypoxia drives fibrotic remodeling).

rs2243250.name: C-590T (rs2243250)
rs2243250.summary: IL4 -590 T allele is associated with higher IL-4 production, atopy, and asthma risk.
rs2243250.recommendation: Allergen avoidance; for severe atopic disease, IL-4/IL-13 biologics.

rs77086077.name: rs77086077
rs77086077.summary: BHLHE41 (DEC2) variants are associated with short-sleeper phenotype — homozygotes for the rare allele may function on 5–6 h sleep without obvious deficits. Most individuals reporting short sleep are actually sleep-deprived.
rs77086077.recommendation: Test if you really are a short sleeper: try 7–9 h consistently for 4 weeks and assess. If not a true short-sleeper, prioritize 7–9 h.

rs2854464.name: rs2854464
rs2854464.summary: MSTN (myostatin) rs2854464 — modest associations with muscle mass and strength response.
rs2854464.recommendation: Resistance training + adequate protein remains primary lever for muscle development.

rs10519393.name: rs10519393
rs10519393.summary: PPARA — peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha; affects fatty acid metabolism and endurance phenotype.
rs10519393.recommendation: Mediterranean diet supports PPAR signalling. Aerobic training upregulates PPAR pathways.

rs1408799.name: rs1408799
rs1408799.summary: TYRP1 rs1408799 — affects melanin production. Variants associated with lighter pigmentation and modestly elevated melanoma risk.
rs1408799.recommendation: UV protection; annual skin checks if fair-skinned.

rs2733831.name: rs2733831
rs2733831.summary: TYRP1 rs2733831 — additional pigmentation locus variant.

rs1476679.name: rs1476679
rs1476679.summary: ZCWPW1 rs1476679 — newer Alzheimer's GWAS hit with modest effect.

rs10792832.name: rs10792832
rs10792832.summary: PICALM rs10792832 — modest Alzheimer's locus variant, complementary to rs3851179.

rs7779.name: rs7779
rs7779.summary: MT1X metallothionein variant — affects baseline expression; relevant for zinc / heavy-metal homeostasis.
rs7779.recommendation: Adequate zinc intake (15–30 mg/d) is the primary inducer of metallothionein.

rs2280073.name: rs2280073
rs2280073.summary: ARSE — arylsulfatase E; minor role in detoxification of sulfated metabolites.
rs2280073.recommendation: Adequate sulfur amino acids (cysteine, methionine, taurine) support sulfation pathways.

rs2070744.name: T-786C (rs2070744)
rs2070744.summary: NOS3 -786C reduces endothelial NO synthase expression — implicated in erectile dysfunction risk and modest effects on sperm quality (NO has roles in capacitation).
rs2070744.recommendation: L-citrulline 3–6 g/day, nitrate-rich vegetables (beetroot, leafy greens), aerobic exercise. Treat sleep apnea and metabolic syndrome aggressively (major modifiable ED drivers).

rs8050671.name: rs8050671 (aromatase)
rs8050671.summary: CYP19A1 (aromatase) variant — additional regulatory locus; complement to rs4646 / rs10046. Some testicular aromatization is required for normal fertility.
rs8050671.recommendation: Maintain healthy body composition (≤20% body fat) to avoid excess aromatization; do not aggressively suppress estrogen.

rs2295544.name: rs2295544
rs2295544.summary: Additional SHBG-locus variant from large GWAS. Stacks with other SHBG variants in shaping bioavailable testosterone.
rs2295544.recommendation: See rs6259 / rs1799941 strategies: adequate calories and carbs, boron, magnesium, body composition.

rs2070951.name: rs2070951
rs2070951.summary: NR3C2 (mineralocorticoid receptor) — affects aldosterone signalling; indirect hormonal balance implications.

rs7762395.name: rs7762395
rs7762395.summary: SIRT1 rs7762395 — sirtuin 1 variant, modest associations with longevity and metabolic phenotypes.
rs7762395.recommendation: Sirtuin activity is supported by caloric restriction, time-restricted eating, exercise, polyphenols (resveratrol, quercetin, fisetin).

rs2811222.name: rs2811222
rs2811222.summary: FOXO3 rs2811222 — additional tag SNP for the FOXO3 longevity haplotype.
rs2811222.recommendation: See rs2802292: intermittent fasting/TRE, exercise, polyphenols, sleep, social connection.

rs6347.name: rs6347 (DAT1)
rs6347.summary: SLC6A3 rs6347 — synonymous DAT1 variant in haplotypes affecting transporter expression and stimulant response.
rs6347.recommendation: Single SNP effect small. ADHD treatment is clinical.

rs1799976.name: rs1799976
rs1799976.summary: COMT rs1799976 — additional COMT regulatory variant complementing rs4680 in shaping catecholamine and catechol-estrogen clearance.
rs1799976.recommendation: Magnesium, S-adenosylmethionine cofactors, exercise — support methylation including COMT.

rs2287780.name: rs2287780
rs2287780.summary: MTRR rs2287780 — additional locus variant in methionine synthase reductase, affecting B12-folate cycling.

rs2010963.name: rs2010963
rs2010963.summary: VEGFA rs2010963 — vascular endothelial growth factor variant relevant to diabetic retinopathy and AMD severity/response to anti-VEGF therapy.
rs2010963.recommendation: Diabetic control (HbA1c <7%), regular dilated eye exams if diabetic. Anti-VEGF therapy response is clinical.

rs2235335.name: rs2235335
rs2235335.summary: HJV (hemojuvelin) regulates hepcidin; rare LOF mutations cause juvenile hemochromatosis. Common variants modestly affect iron parameters.
rs2235335.recommendation: Monitor ferritin if family history of iron overload. Limit iron supplements unless deficient.

rs2227831.name: rs2227831
rs2227831.summary: PNPLA3 variants are strongly associated with NAFLD/MAFLD risk and progression to NASH/cirrhosis. rs738409 (I148M) is the canonical variant; rs2227831 is a tag.
rs2227831.recommendation: Limit alcohol; treat metabolic syndrome aggressively; lose 5–10% body weight if overweight to reduce hepatic fat. Mediterranean diet preferred.

rs738409.name: I148M (rs738409)
